il-being-british-colonised-and-coloniser.invitation: We are inviting white British people who have been born and raised in the UK to come together to support one another to explore how colonial histories live inside of us. Recognising the vital importance of addressing the global legacy of colonialism, our intent is to grow our collective capacity to come into more authentic relationship with peoples and communities harmed by past British actions. You do not have to still be living in Britain to participate.
il-being-british-colonised-and-coloniser.methods: We will explore what it is to be British by via dialogue in the whole group and in breakouts, and using various forms of creative expression, movement, poetry, and art where appropriate. Themes to include: * The original rupture with the sacred, and resourcing ourselves by restoring what’s been lost * How we use silence, language and humour mask painful truths * The use and abuse of power *…
il-being-british-colonised-and-coloniser.availability: We will meet approximately every three weeks from 1900-2100 UK time on: 25 Feb, 11 Mar, 1 April, 22 April, 13 May, 3 June, 24 June, 15 July, 5 Aug, 26 Aug, 16 Sept, 14 Oct, 4 Nov, 25 Nov, 16 Dec 2026.

leaders.name: Manda Johnson
leaders.bio: Manda Johnson is a somatic therapist, group process facilitator and artist. She is a graduate of Thomas Hubl's Timeless Wisdom and Collective trauma Facilitator trainings. She is on the TWT Global 2025-26 assistant team abd is a key member if the Pocek Project's Global Social Witnessing team, presenting and mentoring in the current GSW facilitator training. Born and raised in the UK Manda has lived in Aotearoa New Zealand for more than 40 years. She is continually reminded taht Aotearoa is the UK's most recently colonised country, prompting an ongoing enquiry into what it is to be British.

leaders.name: Matthew Green
leaders.bio: Matthew Green spent 14 years working as an international journalist covering conflicts across Africa, Iraq, Afganistan and Pakistan before returning to the UK to write Aftershock, a book documenting the journeys of British military veterans and their families to heal from the psychological scars of war. Matthew is a graduate of Thomas Hübl's Timeless Wisdom Training and Collective Trauma Facilitator Training. He is a co-founder of the Resonant Man international men's initiative; creator of the Resonant World newsletter; and a co-host of the podcast What Is Collective Healing?

il-collective-stigmatizing-of-queer-men-.about: Modern Western cultures are burdened by a long history in which queer folks are othered, pathologized, and persecuted by religious, social, and political systems. This lab addresses traumas-of-stigmatization that gay/queer and bisexual men of all ethnicities and ages experience as an othered group in many cultures. Honoring both our sensitivity and susceptibility to shame, we will explore our inner strengths, beauty, and deep capacity for self/other intimacy. In maturing our relationships with ourselves and one another, we foster enhanced agency to heal trauma as individuals and community.
il-collective-stigmatizing-of-queer-men-.invitation: With the understanding that LGBTQ+ folks self-identify in diverse ways, this lab will focus on the shared experience of those who identify as gay/queer and bisexual men, all ages and ethnicities, whether cis or trans, from queer-phobic cultures around the world. We welcome those who feel called to explore and begin healing the corrosive collective impacts of being socially, culturally, and spiritually othered. Using processes to surface, witness, and initiate healing of shared trauma, our goal…
il-collective-stigmatizing-of-queer-men-.methods: Our shared journey will unfold gradually, easing first into practices that deepen self-awareness and relational depth to build a safe, resourced container. We’ll then gently call in parts of ourselves that we’ve exiled as an intelligent, protective response to queer-phobic environments. As we deepen in intimacy and cohesion, we’ll explore select areas of interest: coming out, family, religious…
il-collective-stigmatizing-of-queer-men-.availability: This lab will meet every 3 weeks (with some exceptions) between Feb 25 & Dec 3, 2026. Our meeting time is 9:30 am – 11:15 am Pacific / 6:30 pm - 8:15 Central Europe Time. ––Scheduled dates are all Wednesdays, except as noted with * : Feb 25 / Mar 18 / Apr 1 & 21* (Tue) / May 13 / Jun 3 & 29* (Mon)…

leaders.name: Gary Raucher
leaders.bio: Gary Raucher is a Marriage Family Therapist in San Francisco, and Professor Emeritus of Counseling Psychology/Drama Therapy at The California Institute of Integral Studies. During the AIDS crisis of the ‘90s, he innovated use of expressive arts therapies in HIV-support work. A teacher of embodied meditation and Authentic Reiki®, Gary feels deeply aligned with Thomas Hübl’s approach to spiritual healing. He serves on the Assistant team with Thomas’s 2025-26 Timeless Wisdom Training and is a graduate of his Collective Trauma Facilitation Training. He lives with his husband, Juan, of 37 years.

leaders.name: Brandt Miller
leaders.bio: Brandt Miller integrates Somatic Experiencing®, breathwork, and collective trauma principles to support healing, resilience, and embodied connection. Based in the San Francisco Bay Area, he draws from a background in writing and documentary storytelling. He facilitates men’s work and leads pilgrimages in Mongolia grounded in reciprocity and the wisdom carried in our relationality with each other and the natural world. He is honored to create this space for queer men to mend collective and inherited fractures and reclaim the belonging, intimacy, and gifts at the core of our community.

leaders.name: Andres Quezada
leaders.bio: Andres Quezada is a certified facilitator with experience helping leaders and organizations with individual, team, and organizational and developmental change. During his previous work as a consultant, he was a regional leader of his organization’s queer group and one of the founding members of a network to educate and prevent discrimination at the workplace in Latin America. Andres joined TWT in 2021 with a desire to understand and address queer collective trauma. Andres is from Chile and currently lives with his husband and their dog in Lisbon, Portugal.

il-indian-and-residential-boarding-schoo.about: This Lab centers the lived legacy of Native American boarding and residential schools across North America, where children were taken from their families, languages, and ways of life. The harm did not end with the closure of the schools; it continues through descendants, families, and communities today. Together we will tend grief, resilience, and memory, honoring Survivors and all who carry this history in their bodies, relationships, and lives. Full scholarships are available to participants in this lab. After acceptance, participants will receive a scholarship code to complete registration.
il-indian-and-residential-boarding-schoo.invitation: This invitation is for Survivors of Native American boarding and residential schools and for their descendants and families across Turtle Island who carry this living history. At this time, this space is held only for Survivors and descendants so that their voices, pacing, and needs remain centered. Participation is always by choice and guided by respect for consent, safety, sovereignty, and community-defined healing.
il-indian-and-residential-boarding-schoo.methods: This Lab is guided by Thomas Hübl’s Twelve Stages of Collective Trauma Integration and held in a ceremonial, survivor-centered container. Each gathering weaves meditation, qigong, and somatic attunement to support the body and nervous system. Through shared witnessing, story, film, art, silence, and reflection, we move at the pace of safety rather than urgency, allowing integration to unfold…
il-indian-and-residential-boarding-schoo.availability: This Lab meets at 10am Pacific / 1pm Eastern time, for 2 hours, on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of each month from February through December 2026. We begin on February 18th and end on December 16th. We will have 11 CTI process meetings and 10 resourcing sessions, over the course of 2026.

leaders.name: Woman Stands Shining - Pat McCabe
leaders.bio: Woman Stands Shining, Pat McCabe, is of the Diné Nation (Navajo), adopted into the Lakota spiritual way of life. She is an international speaker/teacher, a global ceremonialist, a radical bridger, and a listener for radical proposals from Spirit. Her current work is around trauma healing, restoration of the Sacred Masculine, reimagining money to protect the sacred, and participating in Earth’s movements through “Land Back” or Land Reunion - in which entrenched narratives and beliefs are being disrupted through return of land to indigenous sovereign relationship.

leaders.name: Katherine Elizabeth Poco-Enders
leaders.bio: Katherine Poco-Enders lives in the Pacific Northwest on Duwamish land. She is a descendent of Comanche Native American war-chiefs, warriors, and medicine men. She has facilitated groups and workshops for the Womxn’s March and music festivals. As she walks with her ancestors, she has also held witnessing grounding meditative space for families and survivors of Missing and Murdered Indigenous People and for her community processing the traumatic legacy of Indian boarding schools. Katherine has been a student of Thomas’s since 2011.

leaders.name: Roland Guenther
leaders.bio: Roland Guenther is a German born MD who first worked as a surgeon and later as a family doctor, practicing homeopathy. He lived for three years with a Blackfoot family in Alberta and with the Huicholes in Mexico. In the last eight years he has studied the basics of transgenerational and collective trauma healing with Thomas Huebl. In this area he is especially interested in the German-Jewish relationship and the wounds of colonialism in Native Americans as well as in immigrants. He is living on Vancouver Island, BC.

il-the-voiceless-child-lab-global.about: We will explore how voice is suppressed by collective, ancestral and individual trauma; how early experiences of silencing in the family system shape our inner world, our relationships and our place in community. Imagine a child who was not seen and heard, and learned early on that speaking up brings anger, disconnection, and/or violence. Over time, our voices fold inward to be held in the body - an ache in the chest, a loneliness inside. The authentic self retreats into the shadows. We will explore our lost voices by witnessing the space between what was never said and is now ready to emerge.
il-the-voiceless-child-lab-global.invitation: We invite all who want to speak more authentically and explore feeling safe enough to express ourselves. We welcome anyone who has experienced early childhood, ancestral and collective trauma of voice suppression and muteness, and is curious and ready to develop inner resources to explore and be with this tender part of themselves in a supportive group setting.
il-the-voiceless-child-lab-global.methods: We will begin by establishing a grounded and resourced group field, using foundational practices that support safety, presence, and connection. Together we will cultivate both individual and collective cohesion as we gently attune to the ways our capacity for expression has been shaped by childhood experiences, ancestral imprints, and collective trauma. Through embodied practices, shared inquiry…
il-the-voiceless-child-lab-global.availability: We will meet on Mondays at 5 pm PT and we ask that participants commit to attending all of the main sessions and at least four integration sessions. Main sessions: February 23 / March 16 / April 6 / May 4 / June 1 / July 6 / August 3 / September 14 / October 5 / November 2 / December 7 –…

leaders.name: Diana Frank
leaders.bio: Diana Frank has been a lifelong meditator and has been a student in individual, ancestral and collective trauma with Thomas Huebl for the last 4 years. Diana has completed her professional level 1 Hakomi Somatic training.

leaders.name: Marg Tobias
leaders.bio: Marg Tobias is a long-time mindfulness practitioner and meditator living in San Francisco. She is devoted to inner work and healing and is passionate about being with and supporting others on their path. She is inspired by the beauty and wisdom of nature and draws deeply from her studies with Thomas Huebl and the enneagram.

leaders.name: Analisa Baker Perusse
leaders.bio: Analisa has spent the past 2 decades on a path devoted to healing. She is a Licensed Acupuncturist and Ayurvedic practitioner. She has four years of study with Thomas Huebl and devotes her current efforts to understanding and participating in individual and collective healing. She is particularly drawn to explore how trauma impacts our voice as this has been part of her personal journey.

il-german-colonial-shadows-perpetrator-l.about: Collective healing grows when descendants of perpetrators feel supported in facing their own ancestral histories. Germany carries a complex legacy of perpetration - from the Holocaust and WWII to its often-unseen role as the world’s third-largest colonial power. This lab warmly invites participants to explore their relationship to German colonial perpetratorship. As xenophobia and ideas of cultural superiority rise globally, we look to their colonial roots. The lab offers a supportive space for those with perpetrator lineage to soften “colonial amnesia” and reconnect with ancestral history.
il-german-colonial-shadows-perpetrator-l.invitation: This lab welcomes all with German roots - however distant - multipliers, leaders, and inner activists alike:who feel called to explore the complexity of perpetratorship and embark on this tender journey together; who are committed to shifting from a missionary mindset of “fixing over there” to looking within, pausing, and feeling deeply; who feel ready to support one another in acknowledging and detoxing historical harms while exploring insights from the collective unconscious; who are open to…
il-german-colonial-shadows-perpetrator-l.methods: We explore the thinking and behaviors of Germans (and ancestors) entangled in global European imperial expansion, including transatlantic enslavement of Africans, forced missionary work, and resource extraction. We create space to ask: How can the reality of perpetratorship become tangible within and through us? How can we face the role of our country, leaders, or family histories? What is our…
il-german-colonial-shadows-perpetrator-l.availability: We’ll come together for twelve sessions across the year held on Thursdays, 17:00–19:00 and 17:00-20:00 CET: 12.3. (2h), 2.4. (2h), 23.4. (3h), 28.5. (3h), 11.6. (3h), 9.7. (3h), 23.7. (3h), 27.8. (3h), 1.10. (3h), 29.10. (3h), 26.11. (2h), 10.12. (2h) Between sessions, you’ll join a triad to meet…

leaders.name: Silke Breithaupt
leaders.bio: Silke Breithaupt is a Cultural Studies and Communications graduate, a certified Healing Practitioner for Psychotherapy, and a NARM practitioner focused on complex developmental trauma. She works in therapy and coaching with individuals and groups and brings over ten years of corporate experience in trauma-sensitive leadership, team building, mediation, and mental-health initiatives ( silkebreithaupt.com ). A long-time student of Thomas Hübl since 2014, she has completed 2 years of ISTG, assisted a CTFT lab in 2023/24 and is guided by a deep interest in the perpetrator perspective.

leaders.name: Johanna Moss
leaders.bio: Johanna Moss is an advisor in international and development cooperation. She spent 15 years in Ghana and Mozambique in leadership, teaching, and facilitation roles and holds a Master’s in Latin American Studies. She currently lives in Kent, UK, and works with the GIZ Academy for International Cooperation and the Pocket Project. Johanna is guided by an ongoing inquiry into coloniality and how it continues to shape relational fields today.

il-ethics-of-animal-harm-wounds-in-the-c.about: This lab aims to bring awareness to the trauma of farm animals (chicken, cattle, pigs) on factory farms. Factory farming is a global industry that has expanded over the last century through technology and medical progress, raising billions of animals in traumatizing conditions. Animals endure confinement, overcrowding, and painful procedures, leading to stress, injury, and disease. Animals are part of our inter-being with nature. Our intention is to presence how ethical violations of animal welfare in this industry affect our collective well-being. What do we turn away from?
il-ethics-of-animal-harm-wounds-in-the-c.invitation: We invite 30 participants from around the world into this lab, who feel called to turn towards this topic and to explore it in depth. As a participant, you are available to open up to physical and emotional experiencing, and to participate actively in the group process, listening and sharing. You bring a capacity for self-regulation and or you are resourced in your personal life to find additional co-regulation. The collective work brings us often in touch with personal layers of ourselves. As…
il-ethics-of-animal-harm-wounds-in-the-c.methods: We will resource ourselves throughout our lab journey. Together, we will collect information about factory farming and will attune to layers of this global trauma field; our personal stake holding, our ancestors, and our collective social and planetary body. We will lead exercises to receive deeper layers of information stored in us, and will do practices for group coherence. Our intention is to…
il-ethics-of-animal-harm-wounds-in-the-c.availability: We will meet every three weeks (with break end of August) from February to November 2026, for 2 hours, on Wednesdays. Time: 19.30 to 21.30 Berlin / 1.30 to 3.30pm New York / 10.30 to 12.30pm Los Angeles. Dates: March 18, April 8, April 29, May 20, Jun 10, Jul 1, Jul 22, Aug 12, Sept 16, Oct 7, Oct…

leaders.name: Christine Gerike
leaders.bio: Christine is a transformational coach and group facilitator. She brings her love and witnessing competence to collective topics, guiding individuals and groups to integrate aspects of ancestral and collective fields we are embedded in. Christine co-founded the community practice of Global Social Witnessing. She is a graduate of the first Pocket Project Training, the Timeless Wisdom Training, and the Collective Trauma Facilitator Training. Christine is certified as a Co-Facilitator within the Pocket Project network. Originally German, lives outside of New York City.

leaders.name: Michael Grünwald
leaders.bio: Michael is a graduate of the Global Timeless Wisdom Training (TWT), the first Pocket Project Training in Israel 2018 and the Collective Trauma Facilitator Training. He is a Collective Trauma Facilitator in Training CTFT1. Besides his love for the work with people in a diagnostic laboratory, he loves to work with clients on integrating individual and ancestral aspects of life. While being part of the Core Group, Michael conducted a study on the effect of the TWT on Epigenetics.

leaders.name: Gabriela Zagula
leaders.bio: Gabriela is a self-employed pharmacist in Basel, Switzerland. She holds a FPH degree in anthroposophically extended pharmacy. Gabriela is a long-time student of Thomas Hübl. She completed the Timeless Wisdom Training in 2019 and has since been a participant of the Core Group at the Academy of Inner Science. She is also an experienced leader of the practice group in Transparent Communication according to Thomas Hübl. At the moment she is a Collective Trauma Facilitator in Training CTFT 1.

il-journeying-with-breast-cancer.about: Breast cancer is the most common form of cancer worldwide (World Health Organization). What are the personal and collective aspects of trauma for women diagnosed with breast cancer? Shock, fear of dying, anxiety of a recurrence, grief for loss of fertility, disfigurement, shame, stigma. Cultural norms of feminine beauty damage women’s self-esteem and body image. Over giving as caretakers, lack of self-care, isolation, all play a role in dis-ease. The aim in our Lab is to create new architectures of emotional, energetic, ancestral and collective support for women dealing with breast cancer.
il-journeying-with-breast-cancer.invitation: Our Lab is dedicated to women dealing with the challenging diagnosis of breast cancer, regardless of the phase of the journey (recently diagnosed, going through treatment, currently cancer-free). We wish to build a global community of women in a caring and coherent container, as we explore the deeply personal and collective aspects of journeying with breast cancer. Familiarity with the work of Thomas Hübl is preferred and/or a strong mediation/contemplative practice. This Lab is not a…
il-journeying-with-breast-cancer.methods: Our Lab will explore the collective and individual factors that contribute to trauma and growth in our personal breast cancer journey. We will host our physical, emotional, mental and spiritual experience of breast cancer, develop greater capacities to include and witness our own and each other’s embodied experience; grow our sense of interdependence as a community to reduce isolation and…
il-journeying-with-breast-cancer.availability: Time: We will meet at 9:00-11:00 am Denver // 11:00 am-1:00 pm New York // 4:00-6:00 pm London // 5:00-7:00 pm Berlin //6:00-8:00 pm Tel Aviv, Bucharest, Athens, Cape Town Dates for 2026: We will meet the third Tuesday of each month, with the exception of June when we will meet twice. See dates…

leaders.name: Teddy Frank
leaders.bio: Teddy brings compassionate attunement and embodied experience to guide clients to release blockages and align with their natural state of flow. As a Licensed Master Social Worker (LMSW), she has over 30 years in trauma-informed somatic therapy (Reichian/Bioenergetics), polyvagal theory, transformational facilitation, is a Yoga instructor (RYT) and initiate of Swami Satchidananda, and breast cancer survivor. She has studied with Thomas Huebl since 2017, is a Senior Assistant in Core Group, has run 4 Global Trauma Labs/Groups, is a certified collective trauma facilitator and TWT graduate.

leaders.name: Dana Revnic
leaders.bio: I am a Romanian clinical psychologist, born and raised in the years of communism and dictatorship. The traumatic imprint left by the context of my upbringing oriented me towards a lifelong search to understand the phenomenon of trauma. Since 2016, I study with Thomas Hübl, joining the movement of those who deal with individual, ancestral and collective trauma as a path of spiritual awakening. My journey with breast cancer has been both challenging and full of insights and learning. I am happy to co-create a community of people sharing this challenge and to dive into a deeper exploration.

leaders.name: Ntombiyethu Biyase
leaders.bio: I am a South African medical doctor specializing in anaesthesiology and critical care, rooted in a long lineage of indigenous healers. Alongside my clinical practice, I have been initiated and trained in energetic healing traditions. My personal development includes training with Thomas Hübl (TWT 2022–2023), participation in the Pocket Project Trauma-Informed Leadership program, and exposure to the polyvagal theory and family constellation work. I understand the human being as a multidimensional system in which visible physiology and invisible energetic, relational, and trauma fields interact.

il-invisibility-in-the-jewish-non-jewish.about: This Lab examines Jewish collective trauma around hiding, invisibility, and forced visibility, and how these patterns are shaped by antisemitism in the Jewish–non-Jewish field. We explore how survival strategies like passing, minimizing difference, or staying quiet become embodied over generations, and how the non-Jewish gaze—often shaped by inherited narratives that flatten or objectify—carries impact and historic weight. Our aim is to foster mutual witnessing and gently soften these patterns through slow, titrated relational presence.
il-invisibility-in-the-jewish-non-jewish.invitation: At this point in the application process, we want to invite non-Jewish participants ready to explore the Jewish experience of embodied legacy of hiding, visibility, forced exposure and belonging with the Jewish–non-Jewish relational field. This Lab is for those committed to relational maturity, trauma sensitivity, and co-creating a healing field of collective witnessing—participants able to meet nuance, hold discomfort, confront antisemitism, and take responsibility for their impact in the…
il-invisibility-in-the-jewish-non-jewish.methods: The Lab will move slowly in a titrated way. We begin with personal and ancestral sensing around the wound of hiding and being visible within the non-Jewish gaze, then expand into relational dynamics in the Jewish–non-Jewish field. Each session weaves short teachings, guided somatic practice, small-group witnessing, and whole-group integration. The journey builds gradually, allowing safety…
il-invisibility-in-the-jewish-non-jewish.availability: We will meet online 1–2 times per month from February 18 to December 16, 2026, for 16 sessions. Meetings are Wednesdays from 8–10 AM PT, 11 AM–1 PM ET, and 5–7 PM CT. Twelve sessions focus on core content and four offer practice space. Dates: 2/18, 3/4, 3/11, 4/15, 4/22, 5/13, 6/3, 6/24, 7/15, 8/5…

leaders.name: Yocheved Sidof
leaders.bio: Yocheved Sidof is a Jewish spiritual teacher, somatic practitioner, and threshold guide with decades of leadership in community building, embodied transformation, systems thinking and relational depth work. She supports individuals and groups in ancestral and collective integration and attuned ritual practice, and leads trauma-restorative witnessing pilgrimages to Israel and Poland. Trained in multiple coaching modalities and a longtime student of Thomas Hübl, she brings a rare integration of somatic, mystical, and restorative practice. She is pursuing a PhD in Transpersonal Research.

leaders.name: Nadja Lichtenhahn
leaders.bio: Nadja Lichtenhahn is a systemic and trauma-informed coach and facilitator specializing in the relational and somatic dimensions of individual and collective development. Born in former East Germany, she supports individuals, groups, and organizations in strengthening coherence, adaptive capacity, and authentic visibility. Her practice is grounded in refined field attunement and mature agency. A student of Thomas Hübl since 2021, she now trains as a Collective Trauma Facilitator and engages in restoration work in the Jewish–Non-Jewish field.

leaders.name: Jennifer Lees
leaders.bio: Dr. Jennifer Lees is the founder of the Holistic Healing Center in Massachusetts, where she offers trauma-informed bodywork through Network Spinal Chiropractic and somatic healing practices. She supports clients in physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual integration. A student of Thomas Hübl since 2016, Jennifer’s deepest learning has emerged through ancestral and collective healing within her Jewish lineage. She brings a grounded, compassionate presence to integrative transformation and embodied restoration.

il-the-money-lab.about: The US economic system has a particular ‘flavor’ arising from its unique backstory. This flavor of capitalism, both in the US and beyond, lives in us in unique ways. How we interact with money can illuminate how the system lives in us. Our inner world shapes the systems we create and those systems in turn shape our inner world. We offer a lab to explore the conscious and unconscious material that manifests in our relationship to money. Through embodied inquiry and reflection, we’ll surface awareness of how collective trauma shows up in us.
il-the-money-lab.invitation: We invite anyone who wants to focus on the impact of the US economic system and feels like there’s something to look at in their own relationship to money, but hasn’t known where and how to explore that.
il-the-money-lab.methods: Through orientation and grounding we will develop the internal resources to assist our journey. We’ll also build a shared vocabulary and practices to support the depth of our exploration. This capacity building will allow us to build coherence in the field. Our inquiries will look at specific dimensions of money in the individual, ancestral and collective fields, including but not limited to…
il-the-money-lab.availability: All times are Fridays from 12:30 pm – 2:00 pm, Eastern US. February 27. March 13, 27. April 10, 24. May 8, 22. June 12, 26. July 10, 24. August – break. September 11, 18. October 2, 16, 30. November 13. (Possible bonus session, TBD)

leaders.name: Melissa Schenker
leaders.bio: Melissa Schenker is a work/life coach who blends a practical business mind with deep somatic training. She helps people discern purpose, build grounded presence, and make work decisions that feel true rather than performative. Her background includes public policy, management consulting, and options trading. She holds an MBA from MIT Sloan and trained in Hakomi, IFS, Interpersonal Neurobiology, and Somatic EMDR. Melissa has a long term practice in meditation and awake awareness.

leaders.name: Ravya Taghavi
leaders.bio: Ravya is a somatic coach currently training in Somatic Experiencing (SE) toward certification. She brings over 20 years of experience in the financial services industry as a financial advisor, coach, branding and business consultant. Her work bridges embodied leadership and conscious parenting, integrating somatic awareness with professional and personal development. Ravya earned a BA in Economics from Smith College and an MBA in Marketing and Organizational Behavior from the University of Massachusetts at Amherst . Originally from the Middle East, she grew up in Europe and the United States.

leaders.name: Jürgen Wölfl
leaders.bio: Jürgen Wölfl is a psychologist and trained psychodrama therapist. He works in private practice as a psychotherapist, trainer and supervisor for individuals, couples, groups and teams. His particular interest is the combination of mysticism, spiritual practice and psychotherapy/psychology. Since 2008 he has been in Thomas Hübl’s Assistants Group; he has accompanied the Timeless Wisdom Training 3, and the Collective Trauma Facilitation Trainings. He lives in Berlin, Germany. Jürgen will support the lab and attend some of the live sessions.

il-nuestros-cuerpos-nuestro-planeta-nues.about: Sentirnos “separados de nuestros cuerpos y de nuestra tierra” es un síntoma del trauma colectivo que vivimos. Durante miles de años nuestros sistemas nerviosos desarrollaron patrones de protección para sobrevivir. En este LAB intencionamos reconocer estos patrones para completar ciclos interrumpidos y restaurar el movimiento orgánico de la vida. Este espacio no busca respuestas intelectuales, sino presencia compartida, escucha sensible y movimiento consciente que habilite reestablecer la confianza en la inteligencia regenerativa de la naturaleza.
il-nuestros-cuerpos-nuestro-planeta-nues.invitation: Convocamos a personas con interés en reconectar con la capacidad regenerativa de la naturaleza e identificar cómo ese pulso vive o se interrumpe, en sus propios cuerpos y ciclos vitales. Investigaremos juntos cómo emergen patrones de escasez/contracción o abundancia/expansión en la biografía personal y ancestral. Buscamos participantes abiertos a explorar el desarrollo de recursos personales, sintonizando con los procesos centrados en el cuerpo personal y colectivo.
il-nuestros-cuerpos-nuestro-planeta-nues.methods: A partir de la construcción colectiva de un espacio seguro nos adentraremos en reconocer recursos personales y grupales que nos acompañen a navegar las experiencias de fragmentación, estancamiento y restricción tanto en nuestro cuerpo como en nuestra relación con la naturaleza. Cada sesión aportará preguntas, reflexiones y prácticas somáticas que pongan en diálogo sensible nuestras restricciones…
il-nuestros-cuerpos-nuestro-planeta-nues.availability: Duración: Marzo–Diciembre 2026. Encuentros: Segundo viernes de cada mes. Fechas: Mar 13, Abr 10, May 8, Jun 12, Jul 10, Ago 14, Sep 11, Oct 9, Nov 13, Dic 11. Horario: 12–14 COL / 14–16 ARG / 19–21 CET. Duración: 2h30. Modalidad: Virtual por Zoom. Cupo: Hasta 35 participantes.

leaders.name: Catalina Gallo Pelaez
leaders.bio: Consteladora familiar y organizacional, arte terapeuta y facilitadora en prácticas somáticas y movimiento consciente. Formada en Sabiduría Atemporal (TWT) y en el entrenamiento en Facilitación de Trauma Colectivo (CTFT) con Thomas Hübl. Mi camino entre procesos de paz y transformación social en Colombia se nutre de más de 20 años como investigadora de crímenes económicos. Integro saberes ancestrales, presencia encarnada y enfoques de liderazgo ecosistémico inspirados en la Teoría U para acompañar procesos profundos de cambio en personas, equipos y organizaciones.

leaders.name: María Emilia Larraondo Franco
leaders.bio: Psicóloga. Facilitadora de T.R.E (ejercicios para liberar tensión, estrés y trauma) y terapeuta en trauma complejo. Certificada en procesos de Mindfulness para la salud mental y trauma por Mindsight Institute de Daniel Siegel. Consultora psicosocial en procesos de Cuidado a Cuidadorxs para organizaciones de la sociedad civil (OSC) en Colombia. Directora y educadora somática de la escuela Body-Mind Movement Colombia. Formada en Sabiduría Atemporal (TWT) y en Integración de Trauma Colectivo (CTFT) con Thomas Hübl.

leaders.name: Laura Pallares
leaders.bio: Terapeuta Practitioner de Experiencia Somática (SEP), facilitadora de constelaciones familiares y estructurales; disfruto mucho de facilitar constelaciones con caballos al aire libre. Soy docente de Integración Somática del Trauma en la Formación de Constelaciones Familiares y Transgeneracional (escuela ETP, Uruguay); líder de Grupos de Práctica de Comunicación Transparente, y he completado el Entrenamiento en Sabiduría Atemporal (TWT) y el primer año del Entrenamiento en Facilitación de Trauma Colectivo (CTFT) con Thomas Hübl.

il-kollektives-trauma-in-bildung-und-erz.about: Wir wollen erforschen, wie kollektives Trauma die Art und Weise wie wir Kinder erziehen und bilden beeinflusst - zu Hause und in Schulen Wir betrachten die Entstehung dieser Systeme im deutschsprachigen Raum, die Einflüsse der deutschen Geschichte darauf und welche Konflikte sich daraus heute in Schule zeigen. Ebenso erforschen wir, welche Erfahrungen uns selbst geprägt haben und wie sie über Generationen weitergegeben werden. Wir fragen, wie eine Umgebung entstehen kann, in der Kinder sich wirklich entfalten können. Im Lauf des Labs integrieren wir die Themen, die Teilnehmende mitbringen.
il-kollektives-trauma-in-bildung-und-erz.invitation: Das Lab richtet sich an verschiedene Professionen im Bildungsbereich - Lehrende, Studierende, Ausbildende, Pädagogen, Sozialarbeitende, …- und an Eltern, die ihre eigenen und kollektive Bildungs-Traumata erkennen und transformieren möchten. Wir wünschen uns Teilnehmende, die ein Commitment für möglichst alle Termine haben, so dass wir einen gehaltenen Raum für eine kontinuierliche Entwicklung schaffen. Wir freuen uns auf dich und unsere gemeinsame Forschungsreise!
il-kollektives-trauma-in-bildung-und-erz.methods: Wir bauen zu Beginn einen Vertrauensraum miteinander auf und legen die Grundlagenfür unsere Zusammenarbeit. Um uns mit dem Thema auseinanderzusetzen, starten wir mit unserer eigenen Bildungsbiografie und wie diese unser heutiges Leben beeinflusst. Wir untersuchen die Wurzeln typischer Bildungsstrukturen in deutschsprachigen Ländern in der Vergangenheit, wie Kirche, Faschismus, Militär und…
il-kollektives-trauma-in-bildung-und-erz.availability: Unsere Meetings finden immer am Montagabend deutscher Zeit statt an folgenden Terminen: 23.02.26, 02.03., 23.03., 20.04.,18.05.,15.06.,13.07.,17.08., 21.09., 5.10. und 19.10.2026 Um uns kennenzulernen, beginnen wir mit zwei längeren Sitzungen von jeweils 3 Stunden. Die folgenden 9 Sitzungen dauern…

leaders.name: Silke Weiß
leaders.bio: Silke Weiss ist Trainerin, Coach, Dozentin und Transformationsbegleiterin für eine beziehungsorientierte Lernkultur und Ex-Lehrerin. Seit 2009, inspiriert durch Thomas Hübl, bringt sie Bewusstseins-Arbeit in Bildungskontexte. Seitdem ist sie auch in vielen Gruppen und Trainings der Academy of Inner Science involviert. Sie leitet die von ihr gegründete LernKulturZeit Akademie und hat das Netzwerk Pioneers of Education initiiert. Sie ist Collective Trauma Co-Facilitator. Ihre Mission in ist es, Verletzungen des Gewebes des Lebens zu heilen um Kindern optimale Wachstumsbedingungen zu schaffen.

leaders.name: Adelheid Köhn
leaders.bio: Adelheid Köhn ist Heilpraktikerin für Psychotherapie, NARM-Therapeutin und Dipl.-Sozialpädagogin. Seit 15 Jahren bewegt sie sich im Feld von Thomas Hübl, ist in der Coregroup und hat an verschiedenen traumarelevanten Projekten mitgewirkt. Derzeit macht sie eine Ausbildung zum Global Social Witnessing Facilitator. Bildung zieht sich wie ein roter Faden durch ihr Leben. In ihrer fast 20-jährigen therapeutischen Tätigkeit hat sie viele Lehrer:innen begleitet. Sie interessiert die Frage, wie traumasensible Bildung in komplexen Schulsystemen und in Großstadtmilieus wirklich gelingen kann.

leaders.name: Julia Friedel
leaders.bio: Julia Friedel ist Dipl. Pädagogin, Dipl. Sozialpädagogin, Elternbegleiterin, Coach und Integrale Schulentwicklerin und arbeitet seit fast 10 Jahren in der Familienbildung. Seit vielen Jahren leitet sie dort offene Treffs für Eltern und Großeltern. Erziehungsthemen praxisnah aufzubereiten, gehört zu ihren Themenschwerpunkten. Als Gründerin von Nordsterneltern unterstützt sie Eltern dabei, ihr Familienleben bindungssicher aufzustellen und den Herausforderungen durch Schule zu begegnen. Ihr Herzenswunsch ist es, eine (Bildungs-) Zukunft mitzugestalten, die Kinder stärkt und bereichert.

il-was-bedeutet-es-deutsch-zu-sein.about: Was hält uns zurück, die Herausforderungen unserer Zeit mutig und kreativ mitzugestalten? Oft scheint ein Nebel aus Angst, Scham und Unsicherheit unser Handeln zu trüben. Die Narben der Vergangenheit erschweren es, im eigenen Deutschsein zu stehen und unserer Vielfalt, Lebendigkeit und Innovationskraft Raum zu geben. In diesem Lab wenden wir uns gemeinsam unseren lebendigen wie verletzten Wurzeln zu, um neue Handlungsfähigkeit, Verbundenheit und Kraft zu entfalten.
il-was-bedeutet-es-deutsch-zu-sein.invitation: Wir laden Menschen ein, die erforschen möchten, wie Spuren der Vergangenheit ihr Leben, ihre Beziehungen und ihr Menschsein prägen. Die bereit sind, um das zu trauern, was verloren gegangen und zerstört wurde, und verschüttete, zerbrochene Traditionen wieder zu beleben. Die sich von Natur, Sprache, Literatur und Kunst nähren lassen möchten und Wege suchen, ihr Deutschsein anzunehmen, daraus Kraft zu schöpfen und Verantwortung in der Gegenwart zu übernehmen.
il-was-bedeutet-es-deutsch-zu-sein.methods: Wir werden mit Hilfe von Meditation, kreativem Ausdruck, Bewegung, Poesie und Kunst erforschen, was es bedeutet, deutsch zu sein: Wir schaffen einen geschützten Raum, in dem persönliche Erfahrungen, Geschichten, Impulse und die Weisheit der Einzelnen wie auch der Gruppe Platz haben. In Zweier- und Dreiergruppen sowie in der gesamten Gruppe werden wir das Thema erkunden.
il-was-bedeutet-es-deutsch-zu-sein.availability: Wir treffen uns einmal im Monat online, jeweils montags von 19:00–21:30 Uhr, an folgenden Terminen: 23.02., 23.03., 27.04., 18.05., 15.06., 20.07., 17.08., 21.09., 26.10., 23.11. und 14.12.

leaders.name: Ingrid Pickel
leaders.bio: Ingrid Pickel ist Theaterregisseurin, Integrative Dramatherapeutin (FPI) und Coach. Sie hat mehrere Jahre in Frankreich und den USA gelebt und Pädagogik, Französisch, Geschichte und Politik studiert. Sie war Teil der freien Theaterszene und hat professionelle und kommunale Theaterprojekte realisiert. Sie hat intensiv Aikido trainiert. Improvisation und „Global Social Witnessing“(GSW) sind ein wichtiger Teil ihres Lebens. Seit über 10 Jahren vertieft sie die Lehren von Thomas Hübl und ist Mitglied der CoreGroup. Seit 2018 leitet sie deutschsprachige GSW-Praxisgruppen. (www.ingridpickel.de)

leaders.name: Bjoern Lasse Herrmann
leaders.bio: Bjoern Lasse Herrmann ist Unternehmer und Berater im Bereich Künstliche Intelligenz und gesellschaftlicher Wandel. Nach vielen Jahren in der internationalen Tech- und Start-up-Szene widmet er sich heute der Verbindung von Innovation, Bewusstseinsarbeit und gemeinschaftsbasierter Regeneration. Seit 2021 vertieft er die Lehren von Thomas Hübl und engagiert sich in kollektiven Trauma-Labs. Er lebt zwischen Deutschland, USA und Costa Rica und ist Vater eines Sohnes.

leaders.name: Britta Möckelmann
leaders.bio: Britta Möckelmann ist Psychologische Psychotherapeutin mit Schwerpunkt Verhaltenstherapie und Weiterbildungen in personenzentrierter Beratung, psychodynamisch-imaginativer Traumatherapie für Kinder und Jugendliche (PITT-KID) sowie Atem- und Körpertherapie nach Stanislav Grof. Sie verfügt über 13 Jahre Erfahrung in Erziehungs- und Familienberatung und ist heute selbstständig in einem Praxiskollektiv in Berlin. Seit über zwölf Jahren vertieft sie die Lehren von Thomas Hübl, ist Mitglied der CoreGroup, der ISTG, war Praktikantin im TWT 5 und 6 und Teil des Assistenzteams vom TWT Global 1 und 2.

il-the-collective-curse-of-success-ism.about: Many of us inherit an invisible curse from predominant systems and culture: be extraordinary, be productive, be more. Shaped by colonial legacies, economic structures, and family survival strategies, this conditioning teaches that worth must be earned and belonging is conditional. Over time, it forms “successism”—a collective illness that constricts our agency, burdens us with chronic efforting, and imprints the nervous system toward vigilance and survival. This Lab explores how scarcity and separation live in our bodies, nourishing our capacity to be in service of Life.
il-the-collective-curse-of-success-ism.invitation: This Lab is for those carrying the internalized pressure to perform, excel, or prove their worth. In many of us, this pressure activates patterns of fighting, striving, pleasing, hiding, numbing, or disconnecting as ways to seek safety and belonging. We invite anyone curious about how inherited scarcity lives in both body and culture, and who longs for a more grounded, soul-aligned way of being.
il-the-collective-curse-of-success-ism.methods: We explore “successism” through collective trauma principles, cultivating a coherent field where patterns of scarcity, striving, internalized oppression, and conditional worth can be witnessed and metabolized. Through somatic sensing, resourcing, and structured attunement practices (e.g. triads and collective inquiry), we begin to build community based on more soulful values. The flow gradually…
il-the-collective-curse-of-success-ism.availability: Six Sunday Sessions 29 March, 26 April, 24 May, 21 June, 16 August, 20 September 2026 Time: 10:00–12:00 (UTC-6) • Europe (CET/UTC+1): 17:00–19:00 • East Coast (ET/UTC-5): 11:00–13:00 • Mountain Time (MT/UTC-7): 9:00–11:00 • Pacific Time (PT/UTC-8): 8:00–10:00 ⸻ Three-Day Online Weekend Retreat…

leaders.name: Vania Perez Moreno
leaders.bio: Vania Pérez Moreno is a Mexican IFS and Gestalt psychotherapist, Certified Trainer in Nonviolent Communication, and an experienced practitioner in men’s and couples work. He leads retreats and trainings internationally, tending the subtle threads of the relational fabric and drawing on earth- and spirit-honoring traditions. His work honors the intelligence of life and invites deeper trust in its unfolding, fostering reconnection and recognition of our interdependence.

leaders.name: Prashant Goel
leaders.bio: Prashant works in service of healing-centered systems and culture change. He has held board and leadership roles in trauma healing and social reform organizations, including Somatic Experiencing International, Inner Science, and NARM. His background includes corporate strategy consulting and UN systems-change work. His practice is informed by advanced degrees in law, business, and regenerative economics, as well as formal initiation in three wisdom lineages.

leaders.name: Angela Zinser
leaders.bio: Angela is an integral coach, facilitator, and expert in soulful leadership and organizational development. After directing global leadership development at a multinational corporation, she founded The People Network—a collective of experts supporting businesses in healing and development. Certified in integral coaching, trauma-informed process work, and soul-based guidance, Angela supports entrepreneurs aligning their business with their soul. Through presence & attunement, she creates coherent collective spaces, serving the evolution of human potential by living and leading from essence.

il-women-healing-from-collective-gender-.about: Collective trauma, born from the wounds of gender violence, deeply and powerfully shapes how we relate to ourselves and to one another. It influences our identities, our sense of safety, and our ability to speak and embody our truth. In this lab we are creating and nurturing a space for women to reclaim earth wisdom, ancestral memory, and the vital life force of our sacred female rage—a pathway to embodying our wholeness, reclaiming our voice, and restoring right relational stance with each other and with all beings.
il-women-healing-from-collective-gender-.invitation: We welcome people who identify as women and who feel called to explore their relationship with anger, their voice, power, silence, and the impacts of the collective trauma of gendered conditioning. Our aim is clarity without gatekeeping: our social locations are cisgender and racialized as white. We welcome women who resonate with this arc of inquiry and want to explore with us, whether you are cisgender, trans, nonbinary, or whatever your racial identity. As our focus potentially involves…
il-women-healing-from-collective-gender-.methods: This lab unfolds as a guided, emergent and embodied journey. We will explore personal and ancestral aspects of womanhood through our lived, embodied experience. We’ll sense into somatic, emotional, and subtle rhythms within and between us. Through relational practice, meditation, earth connection, contemplation, creative expression, and spirituality, we cultivate our capacity to integrate anger…
il-women-healing-from-collective-gender-.availability: This lab will meet 16 times for 2 hours each, beginning on Wednesday, March 4th at 9:30am PT / 12:30pm ET / 6:30pm CET (with 2 or 3 week intervals between each meeting). Planned meeting dates for the Lab are: March 4, March 25, April 15, May 6, May 20, June 3, June 24, July 15, August 5, August 26…

leaders.name: Rhonda Mills
leaders.bio: Rhonda Mills is a somatic guide and systems weaver for 25 years, who threads love and breath into spaces of interconnection. Her spaces invite ancestral listening and identity healing across race, gender, class, and lineage. She regularly holds embodied relational sessions for C-PTSD, conflict transformation, and facilitates Embodied Social Witnessing groups. Rhonda is white-bodied, cisgender, heterosexual and also queer, with English, Irish, German, Scottish, and Cherokee roots. As a survivor of gender-based violence, Rhonda is honored to co-hold this lab space of sacred reclamation.

leaders.name: Esther Rosen-Bernays
leaders.bio: More than ever before, I feel a call to find my voice and speak truth to power. More than ever, I long to beckon my sisters to join me on this journey, reaching deep and far, so that our voices may ripple outward with potent grace. As a somatically oriented psychotherapist raised in Switzerland, I have spent decades walking alongside individuals in intimate healing. Now, I am deeply grateful for this doorway into the wider fray—a chance to allow our healing to be inspired and nurtured by a communal space fueling our healing and blossoming together.

il-loss-of-a-child.about: This lab is for women who have experienced the loss of a child. This is a profound trauma that touches every dimension of life. Many cultures lack the ability to support the depth of grief accompanying child loss. While each mother has a unique story, many of the same emotions and experiences are shared, such as isolation. We will co-create a space to grieve and to presence our current experience of the loss. We will access our ancestral heritages, and uncover our own resilience. The intention is for a community of women to form as a supportive refuge for processing and integrating our loss.
il-loss-of-a-child.invitation: This lab is intended for women who have lost a child of any age at any point in their lives and who wish to form a community with others who have also experienced this trauma. In addition to the lab sessions, participants will join weekly triads to deepen their learning and support one another. Although this process may be difficult, it is our hope that doing it in community will foster personal healing and begin to address the collective trauma layers often obscured by the personal pain that…
il-loss-of-a-child.methods: This 10-month lab supports mothers navigating child loss through the Collective Trauma Integration Process (CTIP). Participants move at their own pace, building capacity through presencing, sharing their stories, attunement, and shared witnessing. We will co-create a refuge where we can address the silence and isolation that often accompanies such traumatic loss. We will cultivate resources…
il-loss-of-a-child.availability: Monthly meetings will be held on the fourth Friday of each month for two hours, with two additional 3-hour sessions on May 8 and November 6. Dates: February 27, 2026 ; March 27, 2026; April 24, 2026; *May 8, 2026 (3-hour session); May 22, 2026; June 26, 2026; August 28, 2026; September 25, 2026…

leaders.name: Debbie Ezersky
leaders.bio: Debbie Ezersky has been studying with Thomas since 2020. This workshop is the offering that she wished she had had years ago after the death of her own daughter, Rose. She works as a Disability Specialist at Santa Rosa Junior College and previously worked as a clinical social worker in a psychiatric hospital in Philadelphia. She loves to travel and explore food, culture and nature around the globe. She has studied Spanish in Spain and Latin America, and is fluent in American Sign Language. Debbie has two grown sons and lives in San Francisco with her partner, and dog Bella.

leaders.name: Silvia Costa Pasquini
leaders.bio: Silvia was born in Brazil and has been living in the U.S. since 1998, She is a mother of two grown children and a lifelong community builder. Her years supporting families, volunteering and leading the Elmbrook Parent Network organization shaped her deep respect for each person’s lived experience. A dedicated student and practitioner of Mindfulness Meditation since 2014 and a graduate of Thomas Hübl’s Collective Trauma Facilitation Training, she brings steady presence, compassion, and care to every group she serves. She is committed to fostering spaces where all feel safe and supported.

il-south-asians-decolonizing-a-history-o.about: We’ll explore how centuries of empire—especially British rule and its exit—sheared the interwoven cultural fabric of South Asian communities, reshaping identities, power and relationship to the subcontinent’s rich spiritual tradition. Generations endured subjugation, partitions, displacement, scarcity, and violence with little space to grieve what was lost or re-connect to ancestral practices. Today, these imprints live on in us. This lab invites us to notice how these collective wounds shape our sense of home, self, belonging, and connection to our roots today.
il-south-asians-decolonizing-a-history-o.invitation: The South Asian (SA) identity includes people with ancestry from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, as well as their global diaspora. These are communities shaped today by historical traumas that came from empires, colonial subjugation, displacement, and political polarization. If this is an aspect of your lineage, join us. Requirements: 1)ancestry from SA; 2)curiosity about the complexity of your identity; 3)willingness to respect our diverse…
il-south-asians-decolonizing-a-history-o.methods: This lab offers a guided exploration into our cultural inheritance shaped by the 19th–20th centuries. Through learning and sharing family stories, we’ll presence the human tragedy, violence, displacement, scarcity, and the loss of close-knit cultures that gave rise to new national identities. Together we’ll explore how these histories shape our identities now, attitudes towards each other…
il-south-asians-decolonizing-a-history-o.availability: Saturdays: March 14*, April 4, April 25, May 23*, June 13, July 11, Aug 1, Aug 22, Sept 12, Oct 10* from 8:00-10:00am PT, 11:00-1:00pm ET, 16:00-18:00pm UK, 17:00-19:00 CET. For IST, 9:30-11:30pm through March, 8:30-10:30pm from April onwards. (*)Note: the first, ~half way & last sessions meet for…

leaders.name: Ruchi Puri
leaders.bio: Ruchi Puri, MD, is an Ob/Gyn in California integrating a diversity of healing modalities into her work and teaching of Be•ology, a holistic health paradigm. She is at the intersection of East & West Medicine, somatically & spiritually oriented, and encompasses the spectrum of trauma from conception to collective. Over 25 years, she has supported communities living with trauma across the US, Middle East, Africa, and Asia. She spent over a year on pilgrimage to South Asia’s sacred sites of feminine worship transcending the region's religious identities. Learn more: https://ruchipuri.com/about/

leaders.name: Monica Murarka
leaders.bio: Monica Murarka is a Somatic Coach, Bodyworker, Leadership Facilitator & Trauma-Informed Consultant focused on leadership development and OD/culture. She’s consulted Fortune 500 companies while working at Towers Perrin, McKinsey & Company & Mobius Executive Leadership. She founded Amplify Yourself, a boutique firm focused on healing arts, coaching, bodywork and facilitation. She brings her passion for consciousness, mysticism, ancestral healing, energy practices, somatic experiencing and collective trauma healing into her life’s work. Learn more: https://www.linkedin.com/in/monicamurarka

leaders.name: Our Heritage
leaders.bio: Ruchi is Punjabi and born in the US. Her parents are 1947 Partition Survivors, displaced from Lahore to Delhi and then becoming part of the diaspora in the States. In 2025, she & her mom returned to their ancestral homes in Lahore. She’s devoted the last decade to integrating the ancestral and collective forces shaping her. Monica is Marwari originally from Rajasthan. Her parents immigrated from Calcutta & Kanpur to the US, where Monica was born. She lives in the San Francisco Bay Area, though spends ~4 months a year in India visiting family and studying Somatic Experiencing in Rishikesh.

il-restory-ing-wholeness-through-the-sac.about: How do patriarchal wounds live in the female body? Due to gender conditioning, what parts of ourselves have we had to split off and exile to fit into social roles and find belonging? This lab is a nine-month gestation to heal the fragmented self and re-story the sacred feminine into our lives, coming home to a natural sense of authenticity and wholeness. Using the wisdom of nature as our guide, we will flow through seasonal and developmental cycles to integrate the shadow and wounded parts of ourselves into a fresh narrative of possibility. Together, let’s rewild the soul.
il-restory-ing-wholeness-through-the-sac.invitation: This online lab is designed for women of any and all backgrounds, inclusive of cis-gender, non-binary, and trans femme. We are open to diverse perspectives and intersectional discussions, while also acknowledging our limitations as a team of cis-gender white women.
il-restory-ing-wholeness-through-the-sac.methods: This lab will provide a womb-space for a nine-month gestational cycle to explore patriarchal wounding and restoring the sacred feminine in our lives. In the first three months, during spring, we’ll explore coming of age and the archetypes of the maiden and tomboy. In the next three months, during summer, we’ll explore maturing into purpose through the archetypes of mother and mentor, coming into…
il-restory-ing-wholeness-through-the-sac.availability: Our sacred circle will gather the second Thursday of each month, from March to November for two and a half (2.5) hours. We will end with a closing ritual for one and a half (1.5) hours in December, to celebrate and harvest the fruits of our journey together. Our online meetings will take place by…

leaders.name: Jennifer Edson
leaders.bio: I am a facilitator of group dynamics and an explorer of consciousness, right relations, nature, sacred ways of being, and love. My life journey and adventures down the archaeological layers of trauma, whether direct wounding experiences or what was absorbed from the ancestral and collective layers, has been shaped through formal study, embodied somatic practices, and my work with genocide survivors, incarcerated men and women, and members of marginalized communities. My life intention is to utilize my lived experiences and wisdom to be of service to love, freedom, wholeness, and truth.

leaders.name: Laura Northrop
leaders.bio: I am a contemplatively trained, trauma-informed therapist and couples counselor. I have spent the past four years immersed in Thomas Hübl’s Timeless Wisdom Training and collective trauma work. Rooted in Colorado for the past 20 years, I live with my two sons. I bridge depth psychology, somatic awareness, and wisdom traditions to explore the restoration of the heart. My work supports individuals and groups, integrating shadow and exiled parts, and restoring connection to the natural intelligence of body and soul, inviting a renewed sense of possibility and sacred wholeness.

leaders.name: Holly Gayley
leaders.bio: I come to collective trauma facilitation as a longtime educator, writer, and meditator. My area of research is women, gender, and sexuality in Buddhism. Socialized into a colonial academic system, I have been caught up in writing about these topics in other cultures. Only recently, through engaging my own shadow and the “dark lake” of patriarchy, have I dared to speak in the first-person feminist voice about abuse and collective trauma in my spiritual tradition as both a survivor and dharma teacher. I am committed to empowering younger womxn to find their voice and path to wholeness.

il-family-estrangement-as-a-collective-t.about: Family Estrangement is an ambiguous loss where someone we love is physically alive but relationally absent. This gray zone grief often goes unrecognized in our culture. Millions of people across the globe suffer this type of isolating relational trauma. Most estrangements arise through a combination of temperament, social influences, developmental traumas, and the collision of narratives about the past. This type of trauma requires relational healing within an ecosystem of validation and support. Together we will explore the pathways of estrangement and reconciliation as change is possible.
il-family-estrangement-as-a-collective-t.invitation: We are inviting anyone who is curious about family estrangement, or who has personal experience with family estrangement and desires a safe place to explore and deepen awareness of feelings, thoughts, and sensations as they arise in relation to the grief, isolation, and shame of estrangement. This lab will be helpful for people who want to deepen their capacity for intimacy with themselves and others as we explore the relational rupture of family estrangement as a collective trauma pattern.
il-family-estrangement-as-a-collective-t.methods: The lab will be a place where you and your story are welcomed and will be gently received. We will follow in the footsteps of Thomas Hübl’s teachings on integrating fragmentation in our relationships. Our flow will begin with resourcing, meeting people where they are, exploring our stories, listening to the group, reflecting on our experiences, and learning new ways of being in relation. We begin…
il-family-estrangement-as-a-collective-t.availability: Meetings on Fridays at 10:00am L.A. / 1:00pm N.Y. / 7:00pm Berlin * Weekly meetings of 90 minutes for the first month to establish resourcing, [February 20, 27, March 6, 13] then meet for 2 hours every 3 weeks thereafter. [April 3, 24, May 15, June 5, 26, July 17, August 7, 28, September 18…

leaders.name: Karen Forsthoff
leaders.bio: Karen Forsthoff is a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in San Francisco, California. She began her studies with Thomas Hubl in 2019 and is a graduate of Timeless Wisdom Training and Collective Trauma Facilitation Training. That work inspired and motivated her to reach out to estranged relatives within the US and Germany. Her pathway to reconciliation with lost cousins rekindled her sense of belonging. Shining light on the epidemic of Family Estrangement and supporting others on this journey led to her proposing this lab.

leaders.name: Steven Shumborski
leaders.bio: Steven is Trailmaster with Mountain Bluebird Trails Conservation Society, driving backroads, installing & maintaining nesting boxes for bluebirds in Southern Alberta, Canada. Steven was born into family estrangement and was left in the hospital with meningitis for a month at 3 months old. He has spent a lifetime searching. An evolving sequence of events and study led to collective Trauma Facilitator training and co-facilitating this Lab. Steven’s academic training is in Engineering, resonating with a family experience devoid of feeling. Receiving & being received is his ongoing journey.

leaders.name: Lee Lahoud
leaders.bio: Lee was born into a lineage of Family estrangement spanning generations. It includes her family of origin and her immediate family. Lee’s hope is to bring awareness into this dark pattern in her family, so that it will not impact her grandchildren as painfully at it has those of us living through it. Lee’s spiritual journey began with her father’s suicide when she was 11 years old. It continues to be the fuel that drives her search for meaning and purpose. Lee began studying with Thomas Hübl in 2020 and was part of the 2022-2023 Timeless Wisdom Training which led to this lab.

il-el-dolor-de-la-emigracion-latinoameri.about: Al dejar nuestros países de origen, ya sea por necesidad o en busca de nuevas oportunidades, nuestro sentido de identidad se desarraiga y da lugar a una identidad que “no es de aquí ni de allá”. Como resultado, el sentido de pertenencia se disloca, apareciendo un vacío interior y un sentimiento de aislamiento. Al mismo tiempo, al vivir fuera de la cultura en la que crecimos, emergen patrones que antes no eran visibles. Este programa ofrece la oportunidad de trabajar las experiencias personales de forma colectiva. En comunidad, crearemos un contenedor para observar y asimilar lo que solos no podemos.
il-el-dolor-de-la-emigracion-latinoameri.invitation: Invitamos a Latinoamericanos que viven fuera de su país de origen que desean explorar su experiencia migratoria de manera profunda y colectiva. Trabajaremos el sentido de pertenencia, observando las heridas y descubriendo la sabiduría que emerge en comunidad. Crearemos un espacio para presenciar nuestras experiencias, y atender aquello que con la evolución de nuestro trabajo interior se vuelve visible.
il-el-dolor-de-la-emigracion-latinoameri.methods: Este programa será un espacio relacional para la exploración, digestión e integración de historias de emigración de latinoamericanos que viven en el exterior. Aplicaremos principios de las enseñanzas en Trauma Colectivo de Thomas Hübl del Ser, Pertenecer y Trascender. Co-crearemos un contenedor para presenciar, sentir e integrar las capas visibles e invisibles de la emigración. Presenciaremos el…
il-el-dolor-de-la-emigracion-latinoameri.availability: Serán de tres sesiones inmersivas de tres horas y media, y nueve sesiones de hora y media que están programadas a lo largo de diez meses. Horario: 12 pm PT / 8 pm CET (tener en cuenta cambios por horario de verano/invierno que pueda haber, y considerar que para personas que viven en otros husos…

leaders.name: Cynthia Luna
leaders.bio: Cynthia Luna es coach de liderazgo y facilitadora de procesos de trauma colectivo. Nació y creció en la Ciudad de México y ha vivido en Europa y Estados Unidos por más de 25 años. Además de tener una Maestría en Negocios y Desarrollo Organizacional y ser coach integral certificada, tiene una formación profunda en psicología, espiritualidad y desarrollo humano. Esta combinación le ha permitido por más de dos décadas facilitar procesos transformacionales en ecosistemas tanto personales como colectivos, con cambios que son percibibles en el largo plazo.

leaders.name: Vivianna Rodriguez Carreon
leaders.bio: Vivianna Rodriguez Carreon es peruana y vive en Australia. Académica, autora y facilitadora, su libro Agencia en la Pobreza y la Guerra surge de su doctorado en Paz y Conflictos. Desde hace más de dos décadas explora la paz interior, el desarrollo humano y la agencia colectiva en contextos de adversidad. Formada por Thomas Hübl desde el 2020, y acreditada como facilitadora por el Presencing Institute, ha facilitado espacios globales. Su experiencia enseñando Psicología de la Paz Interior nutre su capacidad para crear espacios donde las memorias migratorias se integran de forma colectiva.

il-the-living-legacy-of-dictatorship.about: This lab explores the trauma of 20th-century authoritarianism. Using the Soviet legacy of colonization, repression, and forced assimilation as a starting point, we investigate dictatorship as an historical system, how the trauma of dictatorship is transmitted across generations and societies, and how these imprints and traumas continue in the 21st century. We also look for the unresolved collective traumas that lead to authoritarianism as well as shared patterns of dictatorship across times and places, with a special emphasis on the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe.
il-the-living-legacy-of-dictatorship.invitation: We invite participants with a range of experiences of dictatorship, from direct lived experience to familial and ancestral memory or resonance with dictatorship globally. In the service of collective healing, we balance witnessing painful histories with methods for grounding experience, resourcing participants, and growing relational coherence. In this way, our work together facilitates greater awareness and resilience, supports individuals in digesting personal and collective trauma, and…
il-the-living-legacy-of-dictatorship.methods: This lab explores the symptoms of dictatorship that live in us long after regimes collapse. Through somatic practices, relational attunement, and shared reflection, participants will learn to recognize the effects of dictatorship in their lives and relationships today. The facilitators’ experiences in Ukraine and Albania help participants connect individual experiences to the collective…
il-the-living-legacy-of-dictatorship.availability: Our lab will begin the week of 23 February and run through the last week of December 2026. We plan 15 meetings, meeting approximately every 3 weeks. Once participants are accepted into the lab, we will set specific dates based on what works best for the whole group. Meetings take place via zoom.

leaders.name: Dasha Gaian
leaders.bio: I am a trauma-informed coach, facilitator, and collective trauma practitioner with a multidisciplinary and multicultural background. Born and raised in Soviet-era Ukraine, I bring lived insight into how authoritarian systems shape individuals and societies. Drawing on neuroscience, somatic awareness, and systems thinking, I support individuals and groups in navigating and integrating personal, transgenerational, and collective layers while fostering resilience, coherence, and embodied leadership.

leaders.name: Lori Amy
leaders.bio: As a professor specializing in memory and trauma studies, I spent 2 decades bringing real-world problems into the classroom and education into the public sphere. As a Fulbright Scholar in Albania, I worked with former political prisoners under Albania’s communist dictatorship, which led me to work with civil society to heal wounds of war and dictatorship in the Western Balkans. As a trauma-informed consultant and coach trained in Collective Trauma Facilitation, I now work with clients to find the opportunity in crisis, the wisdom in the wound, and the hope that helps us heal.

leaders.name: Daria Yemets
leaders.bio: Somatic and trauma-informed psychologist and psychotherapist. Having completed a year-long professional training in Compassionate Inquiry, I integrate this approach with psychodrama, mindfulness-based stress reduction, and other experiential methodologies that support clients in reclaiming their agency, creativity, and vitality.

il-earthbound-lab-collective-trauma-lodg.about: Anchored in deep, generous Land, this lab invites us to sit with the collective trauma (CT) embedded in place— the unresolved fragments lingering from conflict, violence, and disasters. These imprints can create injurious patterns that echo the very hurts that they are the remnants of, shaping what comes after. Not limited to humanity, these imprints include the Land itself and all beings with whom we dwell. With humility, we “listen without the expectation of being told.” We remember as Land, meeting and embodying these fragments with presence, respect, and care.
il-earthbound-lab-collective-trauma-lodg.invitation: This lab invites those who feel called by the Land—those who feel aligned and ready to unpack with the Land and as Land what is ripe, what wants to be heard, felt, embodied, and transmuted. It is for those drawn to sites holding collective traumas too big for us as individuals, yet are able to be met in a titrated way by a coherent, resonant community. As this collective body—with precision—we become the needle in the Land’s stagnant acupuncture points, restoring vitality and connection.
il-earthbound-lab-collective-trauma-lodg.methods: This journey begins with the Lunar New Year, and proceeds in rhythm with the natural cycles of the northern hemisphere. Starting with reflection, awakening and orientation phases, continuing through the germination, growth, fruition, harvest phases, and finishing again in reflection. In addition to our eight regular meetings, there will be two 6-hour intensives— one in our germination phase and…
il-earthbound-lab-collective-trauma-lodg.availability: Regular meetings will begin at 11 am PT/2 pm ET/7 pm CET/9 pm CAT Meetings are 3 hours unless otherwise noted. 2/22/26- 4 hours 3/15/26 4/19/26- intensive- 6 hours, time TBD 5/17/26 6/21/26 7/19/26 8/23/26 9/20/26 10/25/26 intensive- 6 hours. Time TBD 11/22/26

leaders.name: Deep Land
leaders.bio: Land as self, container, teacher and deep Ancestor— as unpolarized, spacious, generous consciousness.

leaders.name: Sarah Rocha, LPC, CCTP, SEP
leaders.bio: Sarah Rocha was born in Gallup, New Mexico, where her relationship with land first took root. Her earliest memories were shaped by red earth, open skies, and the teachings of the seasons. These landscapes became her first mentors, opening a lifelong devotion to reverence for land, self, and others. As a somatic psychotherapist and group facilitator, she has worked across diverse communities, tending to themes of belonging, becoming, trauma restoration, intergenerational healing, and relational practice. She nurtures spaces for deeper connection with self, others, ancestors, and land.

leaders.name: Amy Ode'imin Lortie, LMT, SEP
leaders.bio: Of mixed European/Indigenous heritage, Amy was born and raised in a subsistence lifestyle in the Yukon, Canada. This relatively untouched land, with a small human imprint was the blueprint for her early development. With this “clean slate” moving through many Lands over a lifetime, her awareness of Land , embedded trauma, and its transmutation, is constantly informing and evolving. Weaving ancestral Land Wisdom and intuition she brings passion and purpose to this work. As a somatic therapist and Feng Shui practitioner of 35 years, she brings embodied experience. Zhawenjigewin— blessings

il-mitigating-trauma-in-your-organizatio.about: Recognizing and mitigating trauma is a core leadership challenge. Leaders are becoming more aware of the impact of individual and collective trauma on the health of employees and the overall organization. Unaddressed trauma has been shown to prohibit organizations from being innovative and able to realize visionary futures. In this cutting-edge exploration, a small group of organizational executives will grow their understanding of what trauma is and how it shows up, explore ways to mediate and proactively address the presence of trauma in their organizations, and personally grow as instruments of restoration.
il-mitigating-trauma-in-your-organizatio.invitation: The lab is open to senior leaders at organizations including corporate, governmental, non-profit and academic institutions.
il-mitigating-trauma-in-your-organizatio.methods: Initially, we will attend to establishing a welcoming, safe, and confidential relational field. We will also introduce several individual and group practices to support emotional and somatic regulation proven to be helpful when exploring this sometimes challenging topic. From there, we will move from noticing trauma patterns in the organizations we work with to recognizing how individuals and…
il-mitigating-trauma-in-your-organizatio.availability: Monthly group sessions via Zoom. Generally the First Friday of every month. Starts February 2nd, 2024. Dates: Feb 2, Mar 1, Apr 5, Apr 26 (not May 3), June 7, July 12 (not July 5), Aug 9 (not Aug 2), Sept 6, Oct 4, Nov 1, Dec 6. Time: Americas Hemisphere: from 9:00am – 11:00am PST all dates…

leaders.name: Gisela Wendling
leaders.bio: Gisela Wendling, PhD is CEO at The Grove Consultants International. She is known for guiding large system-wide visioning and change alignment projects, supporting leaders and their organizations to realize visionary futures. As a cross-disciplinary thought leader in the social sciences, she integrates emerging transformational change approaches with insights from indigenous wisdom and healing traditions. She has been described as a visionary anthropological theorist whose grounded and inviting style helps clients befriend the unknown, embrace change as transformation, and support others doing…

leaders.name: Monica Murarka
leaders.bio: Monica Murarka has 25 years of experience advising companies on business, operations, talent and organization strategy while working at Towers Perrin and McKinsey & Company. Simultaneously, she has invested 20+ years in deep study of leadership and personal development, personal/intergenerational/collective trauma healing, and spiritual and energetic practices through various teachers and disciplines. Monica’s mission is to help people and systems BE – uncover, connect, transform and amplify themselves for the sake of living their purpose. She is currently an executive coach and…

il-climate-crisis-lab.about: We would love to explore how our disconnect from ourselves, each other and the Earth gives birth to the great crises of our times, including the Climate Crisis. And how we can bring deep curiosity, compassion and love to these places of disconnect. We will touch on the trauma that leads us to disconnect and the trauma that grows from our disconnect. We will open to the possibility that disconnect is itself embedded in the stream of the Tao and the preparation for a next level of embeddedness, connectedness and evolutionary movement.
il-climate-crisis-lab.invitation: If the planetary crisis is calling you to stop, sense and allow yourself to be informed by the joy and pain of the world and if you feel curious to explore intimacy as a pathway through the crisis into an emergent future, this lab is for you. Prerequisites: being on a path of inner development, having access to a regular resourcing practice and a support network. We are aiming for diversity: cultural representation, fields of engagement, gender, familiarity with Thomas Hübl’s work.
il-climate-crisis-lab.methods: Both Jens and Kosha have led labs before and experienced the transformation and healing that is possible. Our shared commitment and sensitivity as a group + the regularity of our meetings, will shape the unique expression of our collective trauma integration process. The journey will be interspersed with earth experiences, resourcing practices and participants’ contributions. We will trace back…
il-climate-crisis-lab.availability: We will meet approximately every two weeks on a Tuesday from 5 - 7pm Berlin, on 16 Jan, 30 Jan, 13 Feb, 27 Feb, 12 Mar, 26 Mar, 9 Apr, 23 Apr, 7 May, 21 May, 4 Jun, 18 Jun, 2 Jul, 16 Jul, 13 Aug, 27 Aug, 10 Sept, 1 Oct, 15 Oct, 29 Oct, 12 Nov, 26 Nov and 10 Dec. Additionally, there will be a…

leaders.name: Kosha Joubert
leaders.bio: Kosha Anja Joubert serves as CEO of the Pocket Project , dedicated to growing a culture of trauma-informed care. Kosha has worked extensively in the fields of systems regeneration, intercultural collaboration, and trauma-informed leadership. She grew up in South Africa under Apartheid and has been dedicated to transformational edgework ever since. She has authored several books and received the Dadi Janki Award (2017) for engaging spirituality in life and work and the One World Award (2020) for building the Global Ecovillage Network to a worldwide movement reaching out to over 6000…

leaders.name: Jens Riese
leaders.bio: Jens Riese works as coach, trauma therapist, leadership trainer and social change facilitator. As Senior Partner at McKinsey he co-led the sustainability practice, and supported more than 20 countries and 50 NGOS and companies in the transition towards a green economy. He pioneered the use of lab approaches to engage stakeholders in social change, incl. in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Papua New Guinea. Jens has been studying intensively with Thomas Hübl. He taught on the trauma-informed leadership course and co-led two collective trauma labs. Jens has a research background in developmental and…

il-collective-trauma-organization-its-st.about: Participants from within the organization don’t need any particular knowledge but should be interested in exploring unconscious patterns and learning about collective trauma. We are intending to explore with the organization directly what the focus will be.
il-collective-trauma-organization-its-st.invitation: An organization, either a business or non-profit organization, willing to participate in the one-year process, with at least 10 internal key members of the organization and optionally key stakeholders around the organization.
il-collective-trauma-organization-its-st.methods: In preparation for the lab we will investigate the theme and its history in the organization. More generally in online sessions of 1.5-2 hours and offline workshops we aim to: 1. Create awareness of collective patterns, strengthen deep listening skills, and build resilience. 2. Deep dive and mapping the collective trauma patterns in the organization. 3. Charting avenues for integration and…
