il-collective-trauma-organization-its-st.availability: Meeting dates and times will be defined together with the organization. We are aiming to meet around 12 times within the year 2024 online and offline if practical.

leaders.name: Reinier Tilanus
leaders.bio: Reinier Tilanus is a coach and facilitator with over 30 years of experience in international business, both as an executive in organizations as well as in the role of coach for executives and teams. Since 2019 he studies with and is certified by Thomas Hübl, internationally renowned trauma specialist, specifically also in collective trauma patterns.

leaders.name: Angela von Rotz
leaders.bio: Angela von Rotz is a seasoned therapist focusing on embodied practices such as somatic experiencing and NARM. She is working with individuals and couples in her therapeutic practice, coaching executives as well as training organizations in trauma-informed work and teaching courses on embodied resilience.

leaders.name: Mathias Holzmann
leaders.bio: Mathias Holzmann has over 20 years of experience as an operator in the technology industry from starting companies from scratch to growing them to IPO. Most recently he is working with executives, organizations and teams to unlock their relational intelligence.

il-spiritual-trauma-our-personal-path-to.about: Sometimes we do not feel our spiritual belonging because our parents educated us with judgement and shaming around our most intimate vulnerable way to pray or relate to the Sacred. Spiritual trauma could be anything from feelings of isolation to not feeling seen by family, religious and educational authorities. Through methods of self-regulation, we provide an emergent space for deep transformative unfolding and growing subtle capacities. Our trauma becomes our post-traumatic growth and supports our unique relationship to the Divine. Through the alchemizing of shadow we discover a spaciousness through which individual, ancestral and collective trauma can emerge safely.
il-spiritual-trauma-our-personal-path-to.invitation: People who search for liberation in their hearts, who want to learn to meditate, free from old belief patterns or shame, want to connect with like-minded people, create a coherent field in meditation together as a source of healing; people who want to learn trauma integration for inner and outer transformation as well as basic tools for self-, and co-regulation of trauma.
il-spiritual-trauma-our-personal-path-to.methods: The lab would be divided into four sections: 1. Studying meditation, contemplation, physical grounding movements, and journaling. 2. Philosophical concepts of ethics and how to integrate this knowledge into our lives. 3. Developing an understanding of shadow work and trauma integration. 4. Exploration of how our group field informs our service in the world. We are offering spaces that support…
il-spiritual-trauma-our-personal-path-to.availability: We will be meeting for 12 sessions, 90 minutes, on Fridays, at 10 – 11.30 am PST/ 7 – 8.30 pm CET. Dates for our Lab 2024: February 16, March 8, April 5, Mai 10, June 5, June 28, August 9, September 6, October 4, November 1, November 15, December 6

leaders.name: Susanne Breit
leaders.bio: Susanne Breit is a teacher, facilitator for shadow-work and an alternative psychotherapy practitioner. Susanne lives in Germany. Steeped in prayer and mysticism from a young age, Susanne brings her deep love to her work with clients in individual and group settings. In her 30 years as an elementary school teacher, Susanne dedicated herself to providing spiritual teaching and facilitate education programs in university. Since 2010, Susanne has been a student of Thomas. She is a practitioner in the Inner Science training group, Core Group, team member in the Ukraine-Support of the Pocket…

leaders.name: Katherine Poco-Enders
leaders.bio: Katherine Poco-Enders lives in the Pacific Northwest on Duwamish land. She is a descendent of Comanche war chiefs, warriors, and medicine men. As she walks with her ancestors, she has also held witnessing grounding meditative space for families and survivors of Missing and Murdered Indigenous People and for her community processing the traumatic legacy of Indian boarding schools. Katherine has been a student of Thomas Hübl since 2011, is currently in the American and European Core Group, was a participant in the 2022 Collective Trauma Facilitator Training, and is a part of the current TWT…

leaders.name: Brigitte Kotzke
leaders.bio: Brigitte Kotzke lives her creativity and professional expression in the context of free dance, movement and therapeutic work. As a dancer, dance and body therapist, psychotherapist (HP), psycho-oncologist and yoga teacher, it is important to her to create healing spaces, to accompany people in crisis and to support them in using their creative powers for trauma integration. An essential pillar of her work with people is her inner attitude, which is characterized by her spiritual connection and her interest in inner processes. Brigitte lives in Germany.

il-the-global-legacy-of-the-great-famine.about: Our lab will explore the legacy of the Great Famine (1845-52), in which more than 1 million Irish died. More than 1 million emigrated during this time, and there were successive waves of emigration that created an Irish diaspora that today numbers more than 44 million. The lab is not so much about the history but about people’s experience of that history. What did the Irish have to do to survive the Famine? How does the Famine echo into our lives in the present? How is legacy of the famine different for those who left and those who remained?
il-the-global-legacy-of-the-great-famine.invitation: The lab is intended for people of Irish descent, whether in Ireland or in the Irish diaspora. Some understanding of trauma is necessary, as is the willingness to look deeply into our individual lives and our ancestry. But most important is the desire to uncover and heal what our Irish ancestors couldn't heal in their own time.
il-the-global-legacy-of-the-great-famine.methods: The lab will follow Thomas Hübl's Collective Trauma Integration Process (CTIP). We will create a safe container for exploring how the Famine trauma response still lives in us and how it affects our very being. Painful moments will certainly arise in this work but the process will be guided with compassion, care, and respect. And with a deeper understanding of the legacy of the Famine, we can…
il-the-global-legacy-of-the-great-famine.availability: The lab will meet on the Zoom platform. The first meeting will be on Tuesday, Jan. 23. Thereafter, the meetings will be on the second Tuesday of the month: Feb. 13, Mar. 12, Apr. 9, May 14, June 11, July 9, Aug. 13, Sept. 10, Oct. 8, Nov. 12, and Dec. 10. All meetings are for two hours, starting at…

leaders.name: Bill McCart
leaders.bio: Bill McCart has been studying with Thomas since 2011. He has taken many of his online courses, completed the Timeless Wisdom Training in 2017, and been in Core Group since then. He completed the Practice Group Leader Training in 2021 and has been co-facilitating a group starting later that year. Thomas’s work has had a profound impact on his life, how he relates to life and its challenges, and how he contributes to life. He is deeply grateful for this and happy to support others on their spiritual and healing journeys.

leaders.name: Simon Courtney
leaders.bio: Simon Courtney is a trauma-informed psychotherapist from Ireland. His initial curiosity and calling to explore collective trauma, and an embodied spirituality, brought him to the first Pocket Project training with Thomas Hübl in 2017. An increasing awareness for the need to turn towards our undigested past individually has been greatly influenced by his interest in the ancestral and collective dimensions of healing, using a somatic-based and relational approach in his work, where he is following the inner impulse to work more with smaller and emergent group processes.

leaders.name: Kathy Scott
leaders.bio: Kathy Scott is a cultural activist and creative entrepreneur dedicated to creating provocative experiences that animate the spirit of our times. Her greatest mission is to nudge humanity forward by inspiring people to rise and lift each other up along the way. She is creative director of The Trailblazery, which was founded as a response to a need for deeper human connection and belonging in our world. She is also founder of The Hedge School – an award-winning cultural project rooted in Ireland that invites people on a collective (un)learning experience to find our shared humanity.

il-an-inner-exploration-of-the-south.about: The history and culture of the Southern United States is inextricably linked to that of the US as a whole. Our intention is to explore our relationships – individually and collectively – with the complex archeology of trauma and resilience, othering and belonging in this region and look at how our conditioning affects the entirety of the country and beyond. Through a deeper sensing of how the South lives in each of us, we hope to support the healing of the multi-layered collective traumas centered in the South and offer something unifying to the collective field.
il-an-inner-exploration-of-the-south.invitation: Those interested in a holistic exploration of self-awareness, individual integrating, and social healing through the lens of the historical layers and racial and cultural diversity of the South, whether from this region or not, are invited to apply. This lab is not merely an intellectual exercise but one that involves sensing and feeling together while touching on collective history, trauma, resilience, and restoration. Participants will receive facilitation of relational regulation, embodied…
il-an-inner-exploration-of-the-south.methods: Our lab will follow the cycles of nature. We will include the energy of the seasonal and moon cycles to help support our resourcing and alignment with the flow of all life. We will also take our time, touching into what arises, when it is ripe for exploration.
il-an-inner-exploration-of-the-south.availability: This lab will meet on the second Sunday of each month at 2pm CT. We will begin February 11, 2024, and continue on a monthly basis until December 9, 2024, with one additional session scheduled at some point mid-year. Each lab meeting will last two hours.

leaders.name: Hannah Sadtler
leaders.bio: Hannah Sadtler is a coach, facilitator, garden designer, and spiritual entrepreneur based in New Orleans, Louisiana, where she has lived for over 15 years. She sees herself as a mystic and brings a passion for discovering the hidden wholeness in life to all of her pursuits. Hannah has been studying with Thomas Hübl since 2017 and is a graduate of his Timeless Wisdom Training Program. She was a co-facilitator and organizer of the YES! Southern Leadership Jam from 2016 to 2018.

leaders.name: Kelly Chambers
leaders.bio: Kelly Chambers is currently seeking her Doctorate in Classical Chinese Medicine. She has been in clinical practice for nearly 15 years, working holistically with individuals and groups. She is also a Ling Gui Qigong Instructor, teaching qigong as a deeper resource for patients and students. Kelly found Thomas Hubl’s work after the death of her spiritual teacher in 2013. She has since completed his Timeless Wisdom Training and continues her study as part of the US Core Group and the Mystic Café. Kelly is deeply interested in the evolution of collective healing at the intersection of trauma and…

leaders.name: Clayton McClintock
leaders.bio: Clayton Hoi-Yun McClintock, PhD, was born and raised in Houston, Texas, and currently resides in San Francisco, California, serving as an educator, group facilitator, psychotherapist, and neuroscience researcher, with a particular focus in cultivating group mindfulness and body awareness to support resilience and post-traumatic learning and growth. His father’s Anglo-American descendants settled in Texas nearly two centuries ago, while his mother immigrated as an adult to Texas from Hong Kong, China. Clayton has done in-depth studying and training in Thomas Hübl’s Academy of Inner Science…

il-exploring-loneliness.about: We welcome participants who are on board to honestly explore, feel and experience the textures of their own loneliness. Alongside a connection with your own experience in this territory, we would also like you to have a willingness to explore how your loneliness may reflect wider ancestral and cultural strands. We will look at the many contemporary forces that drive conditions in which loneliness arises, thrives, and becomes embedded in different ways for many people across the globe.
il-exploring-loneliness.invitation: This lab is aimed at those open to deepening intimacy with their personal experiences of loneliness. We would also like participants to have (or be open to developing) a curiosity and capacity to explore the wider phenomenon of loneliness as a contemporary and complex phenomenon in our cultures. Our wish for this lab is to offer an emergent space to acknowledge, presence and own our loneliness, and bring it into relation together.
il-exploring-loneliness.methods: Over the course of our time together, we will titrate between deepening our self-contact and capacity to explore and speak from loneliness, and tuning into collective themes. We will be slowing down, presencing our embodied felt sense and attuning to what is unfolding moment to moment. We will also make space to reflect on our capacities and desires for connection. We hope to support participants…
il-exploring-loneliness.availability: Between February and November 2024, we will meet on 12 Mondays from 6.30-8.30pm UK 7.30-9.30pm CET (Usually these times will equate to: 10.30-12.30 Pacific, 1.30-3.30 ET, 7.30-9.30am NZ) Our lab will have three rounds of four fortnightly meetings: 1: Feb 12 & 26, March 11 & 25 2: April 15 & 29, May…

leaders.name: Miriam Nelken
leaders.bio: Miriam Nelken is a mindfulness based body psychotherapist. She is trained in Hakomi, IFS, NARM and is also a systemic constellation teacher and facilitator. A long-time student of Thomas Hübl, she is accompanying the current global TWT as an assistant. She has been involved in the Pocket Project from the beginning, hosting a lab about emigration in the previous round. She has always been passionate about collective and trans-generational trauma. Nature, contact with animals, gardening, music and mysticism are deep resources to her. Born in France, she lives in Jerusalem with her family.

leaders.name: Emma Philbin Bowman
leaders.bio: Emma Philbin Bowman works as a psychotherapist, writer and group facilitator. She trained as an Integrative Psychotherapist and holds a first-class honours degree in Philosophy and Literature. Her approach is informed by intermingling influences: an early immersion in Buddhist and Advaita practice; a passion for embodiment; a love of language, texture and complexity; and contemporary spiritual practices that emphasize integration, including the Diamond Approach and, since 2017 and the original Pocket Project, the work of Thomas Hübl. She lives by the sea, has a special interest in We-Space…

leaders.name: Tacha Lawrie
leaders.bio: Tacha Lawrie practices a body-orientated (trauma informed) and humanistic approach to therapy, underpinned by a deeply spiritual philosophy. Presence and awareness lie at the core of her work. Tacha is adept at facilitating individual growth and precision work with subtle energy. In addition to a Masters in Psychotherapy and Counselling, Tacha is a trained Garden Designer. Both nature and spirituality are near to her soul. Tacha has been a student of Thomas Hübl since 2019, completing TWT in 2021 and the first stage of Collective Trauma Facilitation in 2023. She is a member of the Inner…

il-a-cut-from-art.about: This lab will provide an environment for participants to work collectively to address and process layers of undigested trauma around creativity. This group does not focus on a particular collective trauma but provides a context to collectively presence and heal the larger forces that impact our creativity. We will look at the ways survival mechanisms have impeded our creative functioning, and the way post-traumatic resilience can be a resource of the creative process.
il-a-cut-from-art.invitation: In this lab, we invite people who are blocked and frustrated in their artistic expression to join us on a healing journey through the individual, ancestral, and collective trauma layers that may stand between them and their deepest creative desires. This lab is for you if you experience; fear, freeze, despair, loss of inspiration, imposter syndrome, and at the same time a soul-calling to create.
il-a-cut-from-art.methods: We will begin by building group coherence, creative resources and personal strengths. We will share our creative intentions and the blocks that stand in their way. The group will explore how our cultures hold creativity, and the places we feel nourished as well as the places we touch into resistance. Our lab will devote time to processes around personal, ancestral and collective trauma and how…
il-a-cut-from-art.availability: The lab will be on Mondays at 8am PST/11am EST/5pm European time to 10am PST/1pm EST/7pm CET. On: Feb 5 Feb 26 March 18 April 8 April 29 May 20 June 10 July 15 Sept 16 Oct 7 Nov 4 Dec 2

leaders.name: Jennifer Krier
leaders.bio: Jennifer Krier is a somatic therapist and coach who has worked in the fields of anthropology, yoga, and psychotherapy. She integrates reflective conversation with body-based practices to facilitate deeper self awareness, authentic self expression, and embodied action. She is a published author on women, ritual, motherhood, and self-forgiveness. In addition to working with individuals and couples in her private practice, Jennifer leads and assists groups, international workshops and training programs. She began studying with Thomas in 2015, is inspired by his interweaving of mystical…

leaders.name: Isaac Shamah
leaders.bio: Isaac Shamah is a licensed clinical social worker, a relational psychoanalyst, a couples therapist, a Somatic Experiencing Practitioner, a NARM therapist and is certified in EMDR. He is in private practice in Nyack, New York and teaches at the Institute for Expressive Analysis in NYC. Isaac has been studying with Thomas Hübl since 2015 and has assisted in TWT trainings for the past two years. His approach is influenced by his 30-year Vipassana meditation practice, by his interest in the creative arts, and by the natural rhythm of nature and the lessons we learn when he listen.

leaders.name: Catharine Anderson
leaders.bio: Catharine is a practitioner, facilitator, and educator. She co-facilitated the Bay Area Thomas Hübl Practice Group for six years and most recently supported Timeless Wisdom Training Global 2022-2023 as an assistant trainee for the Americas team. Catharine is in Private practice in Berkeley CA, offering Somatic coaching, Craniosacral therapy, and retreat-style trainings. Her specialty is helping people find freedom through the mind-body connection. Catharine 's introduction to Thomas's work in 2007 spurred many changes in her life; including pivoting from fashion to the mystical aspects of…

il-trauma-in-the-healthcare-system.about: We intend to explore layers in the health care system (HCS) that are mute, frozen, unseen or excluded and to become more aware and conscious of their effects. These effects may be hindering the development of the HCS to a level where there is abundance and safety in the system, where life and healing is in the center.
il-trauma-in-the-healthcare-system.invitation: People who have a sense that something is not quite right with the Health Care System and want to explore that in a group. People who have worked on their traumas regarding personal experiences in the HCS - therapy in one-on-one and group work. People who have experience in transparent communication and commit to 12 meetings to explore unconscious collective areas together.
il-trauma-in-the-healthcare-system.methods: In the first meetings we practise presencing, 3-sync, attunement, self- and coregulation. We establish a felt sense of our group field and explore sources of resilience (personal, ancestral, cultural). We might meet discrepancies in information and worldviews as part of the process and might touch resistance. Besides listening to individual voices we will meet in triads to digest. We will share…
il-trauma-in-the-healthcare-system.availability: The 12 meetings will be on Wednesdays from 20.00 -21:30 Berlin time in 2024. Meeting schedule: 31.1., 14.2., 28.2., 13.3., 10.4., 24.4., 22.5., 5.6., 19.6., 4.9., 18.9., 9.10.24

leaders.name: Gabriela Zagula
leaders.bio: Gabriela Zagula is a self-employed pharmacist, Ahorn-Apotheke, Basel, Switzerland, health coach, TWT5, Coregroup, Practice Group Leader of the Sharing Group for Transparent Communication® Thomas Hübl in Basel since 2014. Mail: ahorn-apotheke@bluewin.ch

leaders.name: Michael Gruenwald
leaders.bio: Michael Gruenwald is a medical doctor, specialising in laboratory medicine and working in a big medical lab; cranio-sacral therapist, body work, trainings in constellation work, NARM-training with L. Heller, TWT5, Coregroup, 1. Pocket training. Mail: m-gruenwald.1@gmx.de

leaders.name: Beate Küchle
leaders.bio: Beate Küchle works as a social worker with refugees. She is also a naturopath of psychotherapy, coach and Narm practitioner and does some bodywork. She has lived in in an international community very close to nature for many years and she feels deeply connected to the holyness and wholeness of life.

il-unlearning-patriarchy-to-embrace-flui.about: The lab highlights patriarchy’s essence as a power-over dominance for nearly 20,000 years, shaping leadership styles and posing challenges in the modern landscape. The past century’s rapid changes demand heightened response-ability in leadership, creating tension between current needs and historical imprints. The lab serves as a space to digest and integrate this inner tension, offering participants insight into the profound impact of patriarchy on organizational leadership dynamics and our relationship to leading and following. It facilitates understanding and adaptation to the evolving demands of leadership and therefore of our inner structures in the face of environmental shifts.
il-unlearning-patriarchy-to-embrace-flui.invitation: Leadership is an inherent facet of life, experienced explicitly or subtly by everyone. This lab caters to those in explicit leadership roles (managers, self-organized team members, project managers), individuals curious about their relationship to leadership, and anyone eager to explore leadership in a patriarchal world. Welcoming those with the intention to dissolve inner structures and foster the emergence of fluid leadership styles, the lab serves as a transformative space. Recognizing that…
il-unlearning-patriarchy-to-embrace-flui.methods: As trauma-informed organizational development consultants, we have witnessed remarkable progress in nurturing more fluid leadership styles. However, we have also observed a recurrent pattern when only focusing on building new competencies, as most programs do. When participants embark on the journey to adopt these new leadership approaches, they encounter challenges rooted in their inner imprints…

leaders.name: Jana Schmitz
leaders.bio: Jana Schmitz is a trained trauma therapist (NARM) and has been a Student of Thomas since 2014 and part of the team in different retreats, the global TWT and the Spiritual Healing course the most current ones. After having worked in the psychosomatic clinic in Heiligenfeld for 6 years she started her own private practice at the beginning of 2021 and works with teams and organizations in the area of new work and inner work. She recently launched her first online course ‘Inner work intensive’ with her esteemed colleagues Anjet Sekkat, Bettina Rollow and Dr Joana Breidenbach.

leaders.name: Leo Meyer-Schwickerath
leaders.bio: Leo Meyer-Schwickerath’s expertise lies in organizational development and trauma-informed leadership coaching. For a decade he has been specializing in self-organization and healthy leadership, fostering transformative change within organizations. Having gone through several programs with Thomas Hübl and currently undergoing the NARM therapist training, Leo further enhances his therapeutic abilities. Leo is the co-founder of the consultancy Tealbirds, and serves as a co-facilitator for the leading edge organizational development and leadership program ‘Tealbirds Leadership Academy –…

leaders.name: Silke Breithaupt
leaders.bio: Silke Breit is an experienced facilitator at Unite SE since 2014, specialized in leadership training, teambuilding, and conflict resolution for all leadership levels including C-level. Having been a student of Thomas Hübl since 2014, she brings a holistic approach as a healing practitioner, focusing on the Neuro-Affective Relational Model (NARM). Currently enrolled in the CTFT program for 2024-2025, Silke is dedicated to ongoing professional development, ensuring expertise in facilitation and therapy for transformative experiences

il-the-inner-outer-work-of-regeneration.about: Throughout human history we have obviously experienced dramatic gains through many forms of progress, but we have also suffered losses in our inner and outer landscapes. As we grow more alarmed by outer adverse climate events and eco-trauma, we are also noticing an inner landscape of increasing anxiety and fear accompanied by decreasing levels of general well-being. Perhaps slowing down and sensing into our grief around ecosystem decline can help transmute suffering into more fertile soil, allowing for increased capacity for discernment around what we collectively consider ‘progress’ and potential action steps that can lead us to increased trauma-informed regeneration.
il-the-inner-outer-work-of-regeneration.invitation: Open to all participants who have done basic study within the Hübl field and have resonance around the topic of inner and outer regeneration.
il-the-inner-outer-work-of-regeneration.methods: We intend this to be an intimate, transformational journey, traveling through some rocky topical terrain while collaborating with Nature as our guide. It is important to realize that our personal relationship with certain topics may be difficult to contain and digest at times. However, the aim of this lab is to expand our individual and relational capacity (our inner regeneration) as we explore…
il-the-inner-outer-work-of-regeneration.availability: Meeting once per month on Mondays, 7 to 9 pm Eastern US time: 1/29, 2/19, 3/11, 4/8, 5/13, 6/10, 7/8, 8/12, 9/9, 10/7, 11/11, 12/19

leaders.name: Susan Belchamber
leaders.bio: Throughout her diverse career, Susan Belchamber has always been deeply engaged with promoting positive psychological and social change. Holding graduate degrees in both Psychotherapy and International Relations and Economics, Susan’s early career began as a trade specialist and international consultant. Her current research, writings, and therapeutic group work have specifically focused on supporting regeneration and healing trauma, while building trust and resilience. Working with global evolutionary leaders, Susan is striving to help usher in a profound shift in collective consciousness…

leaders.name: Christine Gerike
leaders.bio: Christine Gerike is an essential life coach and facilitator of social witnessing spaces. In her work she connects with clients and groups ‘on the playground of being’ to expand inner world and self-awareness. Christine is a co-creator of We-practices, such as Global Social Witnessing or a Social Architect practice community. She is a student of Thomas Hübl since 2014 and deepened her understanding of intergenerational and collective trauma work since 2017. She is a graduate of the Global Timeless Wisdom Training and holds on MA in American Studies. Originally from Germany, Christine lives…

leaders.name: Renée Soule
leaders.bio: Renée G Soule, PhD, has been developing and teaching ecopsychology for over 30 years She engages environmental crises as a rite of passage for humanity, presaging and promoting a new level of maturity commensurate with the challenges we face and what these crises might invite us to become. Her approaches highlight and encourage our innate ability to connect with and learn from our more-than-human world. This vitality is not a luxury, but essential to health and creativity. Teaching nonviolent communication in San Quentin Prison for 13 years has taught her what people who willingly turn and…

il-remembering-european-indigeneity-in-n.about: European immigrants to North America descended from indigenous ancestors. What happened to the diverse peoples of pre-Christian Europe, and their ancient ways of knowing and being? From the Roman Empire's slaughter and enslavement of indigenous peoples through the Christian persecution of Pagans and beyond, centuries of trauma scar people of European descent in invisible ways. The pain of these wounds positioned Europeans to replicate the same brutality in colonizing the New World. When we reintegrate our ancient European ancestors, we can face present and future from a more resourced place.
il-remembering-european-indigeneity-in-n.invitation: This Lab is for people of European descent living in North America, who feel drawn to explore with like-minded others some of the forgotten history of our indigenous European ancestors; who want to uncover, feel, and perhaps help heal some of what our ancestors could not heal in their own times. If you're eager to expand your capacity to feel into ancestral and collective levels, you're committed to actively listening and sharing in the group process, and you're open to sensing/sharing your…
il-remembering-european-indigeneity-in-n.methods: Centuries of trauma have extinguished our felt connection to our oldest European ancestors and land, to the degree that we believe indigeneity is a mystery possessed by other cultures, not our own. How does this forgetting live in our bodies today—and what lies beneath it? We'll use resource material along with shared reflections, guided meditations, and small group breakouts to investigate how…
il-remembering-european-indigeneity-in-n.availability: We'll meet on Tuesdays, 9 am-11 am Pacific Time/noon-2 pm Eastern for a total of 14 two-hour sessions over the year. Sessions are generally held every other week for seven weeks, followed by a four-week break, with a longer break in the summer. Here are the dates: Feb 24, Mar 10, Mar 24, April 7 •…

leaders.name: Kerry Moran
leaders.bio: Kerry Moran (M.A., LPC, SEP) is a depth-oriented psychotherapist with 25 years' experience in embodied trauma healing. Her approach combines a big-picture understanding of psychospiritual dynamics with a deeply compassionate regard for each individual. She's trained in Somatic Experiencing, depth astrology, Amazonian plant medicine, and Vajrayana Buddhism. A former journalist based in Kathmandu, Nepal, she's the author of several books, including "Kailas: On Pilgrimage to the Sacred Mountain of Tibet." She lives in the Sacred Valley of Peru and in Portland, Oregon. www.innerintegrity.com

leaders.name: Jenifer Cowles
leaders.bio: Working as a healer since 1999 with a personal drive to understand the liberation of self and metaphysical principles of enlightenment I have led a nomadic path of travel and discovery through India, Asia, South and Central America. Graduate of Boulder College of Massage therapy in 1998, a certified yoga teacher and mindfulness meditation mentor and astrologer, my passion is the science of the healing of the wound of separateness and emotional isolation. A student of Thomas for five years and a TC practice group leader currently training in Somatic Hakomi coaching. www.jenifercowles.com

il-integrating-echoes-of-child-abuse-in-.about: The echoes of emotional, physical or sexual abuse in our childhood linger within us. 1 in 6 children grow up with some form of abuse from their caregivers. Parents often repeat what they lived as children, forming a cycle of broken attachment and childhood trauma. Survivors may struggle in life in multiple ways, perpetuate emotional abuse, neglect and violence against themselves or others, and cause further harm when in a position of power. Our lab is a safe space to metabolize these wounds so the cycles of harm and suffering do not repeat – in our bodies, relationships, families, and society.
il-integrating-echoes-of-child-abuse-in-.invitation: This lab is for adults who grew up in settings that, in various ways, deprived us of the safety children need to bond, grow and explore the world. We may have been controlled by a narcissistic parent, or punished with ‘time-outs’, beating, or shaming. Some of us were neglected or sexually abused. As adults we see how our unhealed trauma hurts our health, relationships, work lives and how we may pass the trauma on in our own families and communities. This lab is for those ready to face the…
il-integrating-echoes-of-child-abuse-in-.methods: Together we will enter a process of collective digestion—bringing presence, curiosity and compassion to patterns of emotional suppression, fragmentation, and survival. By listening to our stories and bodies, we’ll explore the burdens as well as resources that carried us through adverse childhood experiences. Together we’ll practice relational attunement, reflection, and co-regulation—so that we…
il-integrating-echoes-of-child-abuse-in-.availability: Two hour sessions on one Sunday per month: February 22, March 22, April 19, May 17, June 14, and July 19. An immersive weekend session Friday through Sunday August 21-23. A final integration session for 2 hours Sunday September 20. We will also assign participants to a triad group for the duration…

leaders.name: Marcela Hrapková
leaders.bio: Marci is a psychologist, facilitator and childhood trauma-survivor, trained by life and trauma-oriented therapies—Internal Family System, Polyvagal Theory, Trauma-Informed Stabilization Therapy, Somatic Therapy, and Working with the Fallout of Narcissistic Abuse. Marci has been studying individual, ancestral and collective trauma healing with teacher Thomas Huebl since 2020. Her work with individuals, couples and groups is rooted in her own transformation. She leads an online healing community and the Nová Psychológia platform, bringing an annual Trauma Conference to the Slovak and Czech…

leaders.name: Joe Snowdon
leaders.bio: Joe Snowdon is a meditator and facilitator. A personal crisis drove Joe to dive into practicing yoga in 1995. In yoga he rediscovered his love for movement, breath and devotional practice. He began his formal meditation practice in 2007. After more than 30 years in commercial life Joe has moved into a work-life that balances his love of meditation and healing with his business experience. Joe has completed certification as a personal coach, as Shambhala meditation guide and as a Transparent Communication Practice Group Leader. Joe has been studying with Thomas Hübl since 2016.

il-unleashing-the-suppressed-voice-of-th.about: This lab is an embodied exploration of voice, desire, and boundaries. We will grow our awareness of how ancestral patterns, family dynamics, cultural expectations, and societal pressures have influenced our relationship to desire and authentic expression. We will uncover and liberate patterns of appeasing, shrinking, numbing, avoiding conflict or suppressing our needs - and how that distorts or silences our voice. Together, we will investigate how our ability to ask for what we want, set clear limits, and speak from the truth of our bodies has been has been shaped by gender conditioning. For this lab, there will be an additional cost—with a suggested donation of $200—to cover the cost of the venue. This will be collected in person at the retreat.
il-unleashing-the-suppressed-voice-of-th.methods: During our time together we will practice naming what we want—and what we don’t—we will strengthen our capacity for building authentic relationships, reclaiming agency in shaping our lives, and expanding our ability to influence change in our communities. While this lab focuses on the shaping of female-bodied and AFAB people, we will work through an intersectional lens that acknowledges the…
il-unleashing-the-suppressed-voice-of-th.availability: Pre-retreat zoom calls will be: 4/9 6:30-8:30pm / 4/23 6:30-8:30pm – Retreat will be non- residential 4-day retreat in Berkeley, CA: 4/30-5/3 – Post-retreat integration zoom calls: 5/14 6:30-8:30pm / 5/28 6:30-8:30pm

leaders.name: Sabrina Hinojosa
leaders.bio: Sabrina Hinojosa is a healer and Hakomi psychotherapist grounded in mindfulness and the body. She is also a certified Brainspotting therapist, weaving ritual, the ancestral, and the realms of the spirit world into her work. Sabrina's lineages include Quechua/Bolivian, Basque, Welsh and Scottish. Sabrina is a songcatcher and a medium for the natural world.

leaders.name: Aryeh Shell
leaders.bio: Aryeh Shell is an equity-centered facilitator, coach, and program designer with 20+ years of experience in transformative group processes. She includes somatics, trauma-informed healing, the Work that Reconnects, Theatre of the Oppressed, expressive arts, and mindfulness practices to support deep resilience, leadership development, and collective liberation across movements and organizations.

il-witch-hunts.about: In this lab, we look closely at witch hunts in Early Modern Europe, which led to 40,000–60,000 (est.) executions, 80% of whom were women. Through this lens, we will explore the role and interplay of religion, colonialism, hysteria, misogyny, and the erasure of Indigenous European spiritual and earth-based practices. How does the generational fear of "being burned at the stake" live on in the archaeology of our bodies and structure society today? Together we will sense how the residues inform our bodies, lineages, and culture, and gently open pathways for integration and collective healing.
il-witch-hunts.invitation: We welcome anyone who feels called to explore the personal, ancestral, or cultural echoes of the witch hunts. This includes exploring feminine power, suppression and reclamation of earth-based or intuitive practices, European Indigeneity and ancestral trauma, the relationship between the witch hunts and religion and colonialism, or the dynamics of patriarchy and fear that persist today. We also ask that participants who apply have an established support system, such as a therapist, or trusted…
il-witch-hunts.methods: In this lab, we listen for lingering echoes of the histories of the witch trials in our nervous systems, lineages, and collective field. Sessions will be 2.5 hours, weaving resourcing, artforms, historical context, and embodied sensing. Participants can expect practices such as meditation, nervous system regulation, relational attunement, and small and large group exploration on the theme…
il-witch-hunts.availability: We will be meeting online on either Wednesdays or Sundays at 10am Pacific / 7pm CET, approximately every 3 weeks. The dates are: Wednesday Feb 25 / Sunday, March 15 / Wednesday, April 1 / Wednesday April 22 / Sunday May 17 / Sunday, June 7 / Wednesday July 1 / Wednesday July 29 / Sunday Aug 23 /…

leaders.name: Andrea Livingston
leaders.bio: Andrea Livingston has been a dedicated student of individual, ancestral and collective healing for over a decade. She holds an MA in Consciousness and Transformative Studies and a Graduate Certificate in Ecotherapy from JFK University and is a Somatic Experiencing Practitioner. She has been studying with Thomas Huebl since 2014 and now serves as an assistant in the Timeless Wisdom Training. She is currently the Associate Director of Engagement at the Institute of Noetic Sciences (IONS) where she produces events that bring together the wisdom of both science and spirituality.

leaders.name: Lysan Boshuyzen
leaders.bio: Lysan is a facilitator, coach, and advisor of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) in humanitarian and post-conflict contexts worldwide, with special focus on collective and generational dimensions of trauma. Over the last decade, she worked with the Dutch MFA, at ARQ National Psychotrauma Centre (a.o). combining in-depth knowledge of trauma with political and practical experience. She co-founded a foundation supporting resilience and mental health worldwide. As a certified Collective Trauma Facilitator, she integrates 15 years of bodywork and meditation practice into her work.

leaders.name: Anne Huhn
leaders.bio: Anne Huhn is a psychologist & psychotherapist for over 30 years and part of Thomas Hübl’s team as assistant, trainer & speaker for over 15 years. She is specialised in various forms of therapy (psychotherapy, behavioural therapy, integrative body psychotherapy, family constellation work, trauma work). In her work with individuals, couples & groups, she integrates psychotherapeutic & intuitive knowledge to open spaces of experiential growth, development & awareness. She develops seminars & annual courses for women. Anne is consultant for the lab & will attend some of the live sessions.

il-othering-the-u-s-political-divide.about: We all “other” in our personal lives in small and large ways, instantly making someone “bad” for something they do that causes us discomfort. Collectively, the dehumanizing of othering justifies war, genocide, discrimination and subjugation. Why does this reflexive behavior remain unconscious and pervasive despite the conflict and suffering it produces? This lab is an invitation to unpack the process of othering personally and collectively, and rather than othering it, welcome it as a once-important protective mechanism that can transform into an evolutionary invitation to healing discourse.
il-othering-the-u-s-political-divide.invitation: This lab is for those concerned about US political division, wanting to explore othering/polarization as a shared creation to be healed. It’s for activists seeking more sustainable pathways for their work, leaders addressing divisions in their organizations, and anyone concerned about the erosion of civil discourse wanting to contribute differently. All political perspectives are welcome, but the lab is not a forum for political debate. We want to unearth and embody the unconscious process of…
il-othering-the-u-s-political-divide.methods: We will create solid ground for our journey - building connection, group coherence, clarifying group agreements, and resourcing. We will explore the ways we other in our personal lives, helping them become less reflexive by getting to know them as protections, growing awareness of our felt experience, and learning to respond from more spaciousness. We will then apply this same process and roadmap…
il-othering-the-u-s-political-divide.availability: We will meet every 3 weeks, 12 times on Tuesday and 3 times on Thursday at 4PM PT/7PM ET Meeting dates are February 24, March 17, April 9 & 28, May 19, June 9 & 30, July 21, August 11, September 3 & 22, October 13, November 5 & 24, Dec 15.

leaders.name: Robert Buxbaum
leaders.bio: Robert is a certified coach and led large public organizations. He is a graduate of Thomas Hübl’s Timeless Wisdom (TWT) and Collective Trauma Facilitator trainings, a Mentor in TWT Global 2025-26 and was on the TWT Global 2022-23 Assistant Team. A key member of the Pocket Project team, he is a presenter and mentor for the current GSW Facilitator Training. He co-led the 2024 Pocket Project lab, “Men, Fathers and God” in 2024 and was a team member for the 2021 Lab, “Healing Racialized Trauma”. Finding ways to identify shared impulses across polarities has been Robert’s long-time fascination.

leaders.name: Bill McCart
leaders.bio: Bill has been studying with Thomas Hübl since 2011. He completed the first US Timeless Wisdom Training in 2015 and has been part of the US Core Group since it began in 2016. He completed the Practice Group Leader Training in 2021 and has been leading a weekly practice group since then. He has also been a mentor in the PGLT training since 2022. Bill is certified as a Collective Trauma Facilitator and co-facilitated a 2024 Lab on the Legacy of the Great Famine in Ireland. He is also a member of the Inner Science Training Group that provides support to students in Thomas’s courses and programs.

leaders.name: Jennifer Krier
leaders.bio: Jennifer is a somatic coach and therapist with backgrounds in anthropology, yoga, coaching, and psychotherapy. After earning her PhD from Harvard University in 1994 and serving as a professor at Cornell until 2000, she shifted from studying cultures to supporting clients in healing and shaping their own lives. She integrates reflective dialogue with body-based and mindfulness practices to cultivate self-awareness, authentic expression, and embodied leadership. Jennifer is certified in Strozzi Somatic Coaching, Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, and Somatic Experiencing, and has been a registered…

il-iluminando-el-trauma-colectivo-de-la-.about: La maternidad no solo refleja nuestra historia personal, sino también el peso de experiencias colectivas y ancestrales. Este laboratorio es un viaje compartido de autodescubrimiento, donde exploramos fragmentaciones y desconexiones que habitan en nuestros sistemas familiares y culturales. Es un espacio para sostenernos, sentirnos vistas, sanar y presenciar nuestro camino con mayor conciencia, intuición y amor propio.
il-iluminando-el-trauma-colectivo-de-la-.invitation: Invitamos a madres latinoamericanas, en cualquier etapa de la maternidad, comprometidas con la exploración profunda de sí mismas. Acogemos a quienes se sientan listas para reconocer heridas personales y ancestrales, integrar tensiones heredadas, abrazar emociones paradójicas y cultivar la observación consciente en presencia relacional. Practicaremos curiosidad, coraje y compasión en un ambiente confidencial y de respeto mutuo, avivando posibilidades para nosotras y nuestros hijos.
il-iluminando-el-trauma-colectivo-de-la-.methods: Nuestro tejido de sanación colectiva se nutre de los recursos naturales, culturales y ancestrales de América Latina. Cultivaremos la confianza mutua para hablar de los dolores de la maternidad que solemos silenciar por miedo, vergüenza o dolor. A través de prácticas contemplativas y comunicación transparente, exploraremos patrones familiares estancados y fortaleceremos la contención y regulación…
il-iluminando-el-trauma-colectivo-de-la-.availability: Nos reuniremos en línea, por 3 horas, los siguientes lunes: 23 de marzo, 27 de abril, 11 de mayo, 1 de junio, 13 de julio, 3 de agosto, 28 de septiembre y 19 de octubre, a las 4:00 p. m. hora Ecuador-Colombia, 6:00 p. m. hora Argentina. (A quienes están en otras zonas horarias, les pedimos por…

leaders.name: Stephanie Pizarro
leaders.bio: Madre colombiana de dos niños (11 y 14 años), coach de equipos ejecutivos, educadora experiencial y docente de escuelas de negocios, con experiencia en prácticas relacionales, liderazgo y trauma colectivo. Apoya iniciativas regenerativas centradas en el cuidado mutuo. Autora de “Al baño María”, guía para mujeres en autoconocimiento y propósito. Comunicadora Social, con Maestrías en Responsabilidad Social Corporativa y Ciencia Interna, y cursa un doctorado sobre facilitación del trauma colectivo.

leaders.name: Maria Soledad Troya
leaders.bio: María Soledad Troya, ecuatoriana, madre de Juliana, Felipe y Mariel, es Coach Transformacional y Somatic Experiencing Practitioner, dedicada a explorar la arquitectura interna del ser humano. Acompaña a sus clientes a reconectar con su esencia auténtica, desbloquear su potencial innato y cultivar una forma de vivir, vincularse y liderar más encarnada y alineada. Con un profundo interés en la espiritualidad, el misticismo, la salud y la naturaleza, María aporta una presencia enraizada a su práctica, entrelazando profundidad, claridad y una sintonía compasiva para crear espacios seguros de explo

leaders.name: Veronica Molina Gerstner
leaders.bio: Médica argentina y madre, cuyo trabajo integra medicina, sanación de traumas, terapia sistémica y salud mente-cuerpo. Formada en terapia sistémica, psicosomática, Somatic Experiencing y Teoría Polivagal, aporta más de dos décadas de experiencia. Creadora de programas internacionales de trauma y constelaciones familiares, integra rigor científico con una presencia compasiva y centrada, ofreciendo apoyo sintonizado para la exploración, regulación y conexión.

il-das-dilemma-der-schweiz-wahrend-dem-z.about: Nach dem schnellen Sieg Deutschlands über Frankreich 1940 war die Schweiz vollständig von NS-Deutschland und dem faschistischen Italien umgeben. Sie suchte ihre Unversehrtheit und Neutralität durch Diplomatie, wirtschaftliche Kooperation und militärische Bereitschaft zu sichern. Allerdings blieb sie von deutschen Rohstoffen abhängig und unter politischem Druck. Sie bot humanitäre Hilfe, wies aber auch Flüchtlinge ab, auch jüdische. Schweizer Banken profitierten von Raubgold und der Handel mit dem NS-Regime stärkte dessen Kriegsführung. In einigen Kreisen gab es grosse Sympathien für NS-Ideen.
il-das-dilemma-der-schweiz-wahrend-dem-z.invitation: Angesprochen sind in der Schweiz geborene Menschen, sowie Menschen, welche eine nahe Beziehung zur Schweiz haben. Sei dies, weil sie längere Zeit in der Schweiz leben, gelebt haben oder sich energetisch/seelisch mit der Schweiz verbunden fühlen. Wichtig ist, dass alle Teilnehmer:innen Schweizerdeutsch verstehen bzw. bereit sind, sich darauf einzulassen. Schweizerdeutsch zu sprechen ist nicht notwendig. Die Motivation, das Thema auf persönlicher, familiärer und kollektiver Ebene zu erkunden…
il-das-dilemma-der-schweiz-wahrend-dem-z.methods: Das Lab basiert auf den sechs Kernphasen des Prozesses für Kollektive Trauma Integration (CTIP) und kombiniert Online-Treffen mit einem dreitätigen persönlichen Treffen. Dieses findet in einem Seminarzentrum in Flüeli-Ranft statt. Das ist der Ort, an dem der Schweizer Nationalheilige, Niklaus von Flüe, im Spätmittelalter gewirkt hat. Kern des Labs bildet das persönliche Treffen. Im Lab werden wir…
il-das-dilemma-der-schweiz-wahrend-dem-z.availability: Online-Treffen jeweils donnerstags von 19:00 bis 21:30 Uhr am 30.04., 21.05., 11.06., 16.07. und 24.09.2026 / Persönliches Treffen: Fr. 03.07. 14 Uhr bis So. 05.07. 15 Uhr; Ort: zentrumRANFT, Flüeli-Ranft bei Sachseln; Unterkunft und Essen: zwischen CHF 190 (Zelt/Bus) / CHF 275 und CHF 315 (DZ/EZ)…

leaders.name: Christoph Häusler
leaders.bio: Christoph hat sich als Schuljunge im Geschichtsunterricht oft gefragt, warum sich die Geschichte wiederholt. Dieser Frage ist er seither nachgegangen. Dies führte ihn auch in die Praxisgruppe für Transparente Kommunikation in Bern, wo er die letzten Jahre als Co-Leiter wirkte, und ins „Collective Trauma Facilitator Training“ bei Thomas Hübl. Christoph arbeitet als Unternehmensberater, traumasensitiver Coach und ist in Ausbildung zum körperzentrierten psychologischen Berater. Er ist verheiratet und Vater eines Jungen.

leaders.name: Francois Michael Wiesmann
leaders.bio: Francois Michael Wiesmann arbeitet als Kommunikationstrainer, Moderator, Seminarleiter und Coach. Seit über 25 Jahren begleitet er kleine und große Gemeinschaftsprojekte im deutschsprachigen Raum in Bewusstseinsentwicklung, Konfliktlösung, Visionsfindung und Strukturbildung. Seit 8 Jahren Erforschung und verstärkte Ausrichtung auf traumainformierte soziale Prozesse.

leaders.name: Liselotte Wyssbrod Ammon
leaders.bio: Liselotte Wyssbrod Ammon arbeitet in eigener Praxis als bewusstseins- und traumainformierte Körpertherapeutin. Biodynamische Craniosacral-Therapie, syst. Paar- und Familientherapie und Traumaarbeit. Seit Abschluss des globalen TWT studiert sie weiter in der Core Group und co-leitet eine Praxisgruppe. Innere Transformationsprozesse und die spirituelle Anbindung begleitet sie seit ihrer Jugend. Ihre Passion ist, sichere und heilsame Räume zu schaffen, in denen persönliche, generationsübergreifende und kollektive Traumata heilen dürfen. Liselotte ist verheiratet und hat zwei erwachsene Töchter.

il-der-tod-und-wir-das-stille-tabu.about: Tod und Sterben gehören zum Leben – doch wo kollektive Erfahrungen von Krieg, Flucht, plötzlichem Verlust oder verdrängter Trauer wirken, wird Endlichkeit zum Tabu. Diese transgenerationalen Prägungen beeinflussen, wie wir auf Abschied, Wandel und Krise reagieren–oft ohne dass wir es bewusst erkennen. Unser LAB lädt ein, diese unsichtbaren Muster zu erforschen: wie prägen familiäre und kollektive Traumata unser Verhältnis zu Leben und Tod? Ziel ist es, persönliche Ängste und kollektive Schatten zu reflektieren, um Endlichkeit nicht als Bedrohung, sondern als Quelle von Lebendigkeit zu erfahren.
il-der-tod-und-wir-das-stille-tabu.invitation: Interessierte Menschen, die: • herausfinden möchten, durch welche unbewussten Filter wir auf Leben und Sterben blicken • Tod, Wandel und Sterben als untrennbare Zyklen des Lebens verstehen und sich im Hier und Jetzt für eine tiefere Präsenz öffnen möchten, um das Leben in seiner vollen Intensität zu leben • bereit sind, sich ihren Ängsten und dem kollektiven Schatten zu widmen, um gemeinsam einen inneren Raum zu kultivieren, der Heilung im Einklang mit dem Zyklus von Geburt, Leben, Wandel…
il-der-tod-und-wir-das-stille-tabu.methods: Wie wurde in deiner Familie über Tod gesprochen–oder geschwiegen? Welche Bilder, Ängste, Tabus hast du übernommen? Welcher Schmerz schweigt in unserer Gesellschaft? Diese Prägungen sind wie ein unsichtbares Gewebe. Oft blicken wir durch unbewusste, verzerrte Wahrnehmungsfilter aus der Vergangenheit. Tabuisierung, Schweigen, Blockaden – sie zeigen uns im Hier und Jetzt unsere inneren Wunden. Sie…
il-der-tod-und-wir-das-stille-tabu.availability: Wir treffen uns an den folgenden Wochentagen, jeweils zwischen 19:00 und 21:00 Uhr (MEZ): Wir starten am Mo. 23. Februar 2026, dann folgen: Di. 24. März/ Mi. 22. April/ Di. 12. Mai/ Mi. 17. Juni/ Mi. 08. Juli/ Mo. 03. August/ Di. 15. September/ Di. 13. Oktober/ Mo. 02. und Do. 19. November/ Das…

leaders.name: Bettina Hallifax
leaders.bio: Bettina begleitet seit über 20 Jahren Menschen in tiefgreifenden Transformationsprozessen–in Einzelsitzungen und als Seminarleiterin für "The Journey". Mit Empathie schafft sie einen geschützten Raum, in dem Teilnehmende in Kontakt kommen und gemeinsam wachsen–um inneren Frieden zu finden, emotionale Freiheit zu erleben und ihr volles Potenzial zu entfalten. Ihre eigene Auseinandersetzung mit Tod und Verlust sowie die Begleitung von Menschen mit schweren Lebensereignissen haben ihr gezeigt: Wenn wir der Endlichkeit bewusst begegnen, öffnen sich Türen zu einem Leben das wirklich gelebt wird.

leaders.name: Elke Pfister
leaders.bio: Elke arbeitet tiefenpsychologisch, als NARM und SE Therapeutin in eigener Praxis bei München. Seit 2004 ist sie Schülerin von Thomas Hübl und begleitet als Assistentin und Mentorin bereits das zweite Global Timeless Wisdom Training von Thomas Hübl. Ihre Leidenschaft ist es, Menschen dabei zu unterstützen, ihre natürliche Fähigkeit des IN-VERBINDUNG-SEINS zu stärken. Besonders in Zeiten von Wandel/Herausforderungen und Polarisierung ist es ihr ein Anliegen mit Empathie ein tiefes, authentisches Miteinander zu fördern und persönliche Transformation zu begleiten.

leaders.name: Kaja Novak
leaders.bio: Kaja Novak ist Life-Coach, NARM-Practicionerin und Organisationsentwicklerin. In der individuellen Begleitung arbeitet sie seit mehr als 20 Jahren mit den Themen emotionale Entfaltung, Hochsensibilität und Entwicklungstrauma. Menschen darin zu begleiten ihr größtmögliches Potential zu leben ist eine Herzensaufgabe für Kaja. Oft genug ist das verborgen unter viel altem Ballast. Ihre erste Begegnung mit dem Tod, war der frühe Abschied ihrer Mutter. Seither gilt zutiefst der Gedanke in ihr: „Jeder Moment deines Lebens ist es wert, ganz und gar gelebt zu werden“.

il-the-interrupted-conversation-with-ear.about: Colonization and industrialization persecuted land-based knowledge keepers, severing sacred ties with Earth. Desacralization - the violent stripping of Earth’s sacred aliveness - created a collective trauma of forced forgetting. We inherited this trauma as ecological amnesia: treating the sacred as expendable, feeling separate from Earth’s community of beings, and losing languages that honored rivers and forests as sacred relatives rather than resources. This trauma shows up today as degraded ecosystems, extractive decision-making, and an inner sense of loneliness and disconnect.
il-the-interrupted-conversation-with-ear.invitation: We welcome all participants resonating with this call of remembering and renewing our conversation with Earth while deepening sensitivity and attunement to right action. We especially invite participants working at the nexus of land and community; in conservation, ecological restoration, land management, and community development, as well as sustainability leadership, social impact initiatives, and environmental justice.
il-the-interrupted-conversation-with-ear.methods: Renewal begins by recovering our interrupted conversation with Earth: Retracing what was suppressed, remembering what was silenced, and restoring our capacity for sacred dialogue as a path towards collective healing. We will practice so through deep listening, self-reflection, somatic awareness, the creative arts, and nature-based attunement. As we move together through this Lab journey, we will…
il-the-interrupted-conversation-with-ear.availability: We will be meeting in 10 sessions of 120 min each 9:00 EST | 15:00 CET | 16:00 CAT on the following dates: Friday, Feb 27th, 2026 / Friday, March 20th, 2026 / Friday, April 17th, 2026 / Friday, May 22nd, 2026 / Friday, June 26th, 2026 / Friday, July 24th, 2026 / Friday, August 21st, 2026 / Friday…

leaders.name: Sally Bell-Cross
leaders.bio: Sally Bell-Cross is a research-driven public health specialist and clinical nutritionist whose work bridges the vital connection between human health, food systems, and planetary wellbeing. With over a decade of experience in community-led health development, her practice is grounded in the understanding that thriving communities emerge when local assets, indigenous knowledge, and natural ecosystems are honored as the foundation for healing.

leaders.name: Christine Hoenig-Ohnsorg
leaders.bio: Christine Hoenig-Ohnsorg is a process designer, facilitator, and coach with 15+ years of experience guiding individuals, teams, and organizations through transformation. She has co-founded an NGO and a consultancy focused on enabling social innovation and systemic renewal. With an M.Sc. in International Business, she has worked globally on collaboration and designed impact accelerator programs for social entrepreneurs and ecosystem partners. With collective trauma facilitation, she is deepening her work at the intersection of healing, systems change, and individual contribution.

leaders.name: Liliane Mavridara
leaders.bio: Liliane Mavridara is a trauma-informed interdisciplinary professional with over 25 years’ experience in cross-cultural group facilitation & community empowerment in the USA and Europe. Liliane consults and educates on the impact of environmental pollution and climate emergency on individual and community holistic health & wellbeing, and she facilitates and mentors group circles that cultivate relational and eco-social skills capacity for sense-making, and purposeful navigation and co-transformation of the current polycrisis.

il-habitando-el-cuerpo-femenino.about: Cada participante está invitada a: Reflexionar sobre los síntomas del colonialismo y neocolonialismo en las mujeres de hoy, y sus efectos en nuestra desconexión, rechazo, violencia y crítica hacia nuestros cuerpos. Explorar nuestra fragmentación y disociación en relación con nuestro autocontacto. Crear un campo de conexión y conciencia compartida, donde podamos sentir, transformar, sanar e integrar partes del trauma colectivo. Conectarnos con nuestro ser, devenir y pertenecer como mujeres, frente a los desafíos actuales de nuestra sociedad. Reconocer la riqueza de recursos que tenemos como mujeres latinoamericanas y seguir desarrollando nuestra resiliencia e inteligencia colectiva.
il-habitando-el-cuerpo-femenino.invitation: Un laboratorio para mujeres hispanohablantes que se sienten conectadas con América Latina y llamadas a dedicar un año a explorar su conciencia corporal, así como a mantener un espacio sagrado para que otras mujeres hagan lo mismo.
il-habitando-el-cuerpo-femenino.methods: Nos haremos preguntas acerca de nuestra relación con: la alimentación, la sexualidad, el envejecimiento, la ascendencia, la Tierra, los ciclos naturales, la tensión y el estrés, nuestros roles y arquetipos, otras mujeres, las transgresiones (víctima y perpetrador), la creatividad y los recursos. Como facilitadoras, estamos dispuestas a transformarnos por las preguntas que este laboratorio busca…
il-habitando-el-cuerpo-femenino.availability: ¿Cuándo y con qué frecuencia nos reuniremos? Realizaremos reuniones virtuales mensuales por Zoom de una hora y media de duración, cada una. También fomentaremos tríadas y prácticas grupales entre reuniones. Nos encontraremos los siguientes viernes: 26 de enero, 23 de febrero, 22 de marzo, 26 de…

leaders.name: Stephanie Pizarro
leaders.bio: Stephanie Pizarro es colombiana. Se desempeña como Coach de Equipos Ejecutivos y educadora experiencial con una amplia trayectoria en Desarrollo Organizacional, Gestión del Cambio y Liderazgo Transformacional, en diversos negocios, geografías y culturas, apoyando esfuerzos de mejora gradual y sostenible que priorizan el fomento de una cultura humana de interdependencia y progreso. Es autora de “Al baño María, un encuentro sagrado contigo misma”, un viaje guiado para mujeres que anhelan un cultivo profundo de autoconciencia, fluidez interior y propósito personal. Profesional en Comunicación…

leaders.name: Maria Soledad Troya
leaders.bio: Ecuatoriana, Coach Ontológico Profesional Certificada (PCC), acompaña a líderes ejecutivos y grupos de organizaciones multiculturales en su desarrollo de liderazgo, facilitando un trabajo transformacional muy profundo. Combina con su trabajo su experiencia en emprendimiento, liderazgo de Coaches, facilitadora de Círculos de Coaching, miembro del directorio de la Federación Internacional de Coaching en Ecuador (ICF), gerencia, moderadora de foros, meditadora, estudiante, esposa, y madre de tres hijos. Tiene un título en Administración de Empresas en The University of Texas at Austin…

leaders.name: Karla Mejia
leaders.bio: Psicoterapeuta salvadoreña, especializada en integracion de trauma individual y colectivo, con mas de 15 años de experiencia en Las Americas, Europa e Indonesia. Terapeuta y facilitadora comunidades Indigenas y Garifunas en Guatemala y Belice. Lider de programas para la integracion de trauma colectivo para adolescentes en contexto de alta violencia en El Salvador y Guatemala, de comunidades indigenas t sobrevivientes de las guerras civiles en ambos paises. Licenciada en psicopedagogía logia (El Salvador), maestria en psicologia analitica transpersonal (Mexico), Certificada en movimiento…

il-collective-trauma-in-our-personal-car.about: We want to explore all areas of collective trauma the group participants and us have encountered in our professional lives. It can range from Patriarchy, Power Systems, Discrimination to Mental Health.
il-collective-trauma-in-our-personal-car.invitation: We invite all people interested in exploring collective trauma from a career and professional perspective.
il-collective-trauma-in-our-personal-car.methods: We plan a soft start by first investing in building a safe space and group coherence so that the respective collective trauma patterns can emerge and a trauma landscape can form over the first months. The objective is that participants identify the topics that are relevant to them individually, but we assume that collective patterns will surface. In a later stage, we plan to dive deeper into the…
il-collective-trauma-in-our-personal-car.availability: We plan to meet every 3-4 weeks in an online format for about 3 hours.

leaders.name: Dagmar Attolini
leaders.bio: Dagmar Attolini has worked with managers and teams as a coach and consultant for over 20 years, previously at the Boston Consulting Group and later independently. She focuses on change processes, corporate culture, communication and leadership – always to change people's mindsets in organizations. Dagmar herself has led teams, managed projects and facilitated many workshops. She originally studied business administration and later trained as a systemic coach and a non-medical practitioner for psychotherapy. She has also been looking at awareness, transparent communication, and individual and…

leaders.name: Nina Fischer
leaders.bio: Nina Fischer is a systemic management coach, generative facilitator and change maker for executives. She has been supporting managers and teams from start-ups, SMEs, and DAX 30 companies for 12 years. Her constant drive for personal growth and development has had a powerful influence on her view of leadership. For her, self-leadership and the development of inner skills is the key to successfully leading others. Her approach to transformation involves not only teaching skills and methodological knowledge but also training and integration for the body. ‘I am passionate about supporting people…

il-healing-german-jewish-wounds-global.about: We are coming together today in solidarity to hold healing space for one another. This is not an intellectual exploration, because this is an experiential process. We strongly recommend that people who are interested in this lab have a commitment to some kind of daily embodiment practice. And that they are familiar with expressing their emotions in a non-violent way towards others.
il-healing-german-jewish-wounds-global.invitation: Approximately eight Jews and eight Germans.
il-healing-german-jewish-wounds-global.methods: We are looking to build a safe container where we gradually sink below the cognitive polarization into a level of depth where we can feel intimate together and process feelings that want to release. In doing so, we will ground the energy of our personal, ancestral and collective past through our bodies. We will explore it in groups of two and three, in group processes and meditations.
il-healing-german-jewish-wounds-global.availability: Once a month first Friday of each month at 6pm til 8 pm CET (Berlin), 12pm til 2pm EDT (North Carolina). Except February and May, both starting at the second Friday: 9th and May 10th. February 9th. March 1st April 5th May 10th June 7th July 5th August 2nd September 6th October 4th November 1st…

leaders.name: Joel Decker
leaders.bio: Joel Decker is a licensed Psychotherapist, Somatic Experiencing Practitioner, Couples Coach, and Pre and Perinatal Family Consultant. He runs groups, trainings, and teaches trauma-responsive therapy practices at California Institute of Integral Studies (CIIS) and John F Kennedy University (JFK). He also assists the Somatic Experiencing trainings in the US and Internationally, and is a visiting lecturer at Diablo Valley College. He works with individuals, couples, and groups. Joel has been involved with Thomas' teachings for 6 years and is part of the CoreGroup and the Inner Science training…

leaders.name: Britta Möckelmann
leaders.bio: Britta Möckelmann is a graduate psychologist, in training as a behavioral therapist, naturopathic psychotherapist and has training in person-centered counseling, psychodynamic imaginative trauma therapy for children and adolescents (PITT-KID) and in-breath and body therapy according to Stanislav Grof. Britta has 13 years of experience in parenting and family counseling with children, adolescents and adults. She currently works with day patients in behavioral therapy training and independently in a group practice. Britta has been involved with Thomas' teachings for 10 years and is part of the…

il-becoming-a-bridge-in-a-polarized-worl.about: How do we take responsibility and find a healthy relation to stark polarization? We are inviting those who feel called to be the bridge in the midst of fragmentation. Our global communities have been increasingly under the pressure of highly polarized dynamics. We recognize it in wars around the world, extremism in politics, clash of religious groups, increasing racial tension, divergent approaches to the pandemic, contrasting views on climate change, and so on. Together, we will examine the process of gently transforming our inner polarized parts, relating to that in our communities, and beginning to impact our collective fields of influence.
il-becoming-a-bridge-in-a-polarized-worl.invitation: People from all walks of life who feel called to address polarization in our communities, to explore the process and build the capacity to stay engaged here, together.
il-becoming-a-bridge-in-a-polarized-worl.methods: We will begin our journey with learning who’s in the room and establishing a foundation to work together. Throughout the year we will look at topics that feel alive with our group participants, whilst keeping the emphasis on our process of meeting polarization in a gentle, precise way.
il-becoming-a-bridge-in-a-polarized-worl.availability: We will meet for two hours on the Second or Third Sunday of the Month, 2024 January 21st 8-10pm CET (alternate start time) February 18th 7-9pm CET March 10th 7pm CET April 14th 8pm CET (alternate start time) May 19th 7pm CET June 9th 7pm CET July 21st 7p CET August 11th 7pm CET September 8th 7pm…

leaders.name: Odile Del Giudice
leaders.bio: Odile Del Giudice works as a somatic integration coach, group facilitator, and theatre artist. She is a senior participant and assistant in the Academy of Inner Science, training under the guidance of Thomas Hübl since the Spring of 2011, having completed numerous courses including the Timeless Wisdom Training, Collective Trauma Facilitator Training and the Pocket Project Training on Integrating Collective and Intergenerational Trauma. Her aim is to facilitate powerful containers for healing and transformation, expanding our connection to our true nature, and furthering our embodied impact in…

leaders.name: Andrea Livingston
leaders.bio: Andrea Livingston has been a dedicated student of healing and transformation of both individual and collective consciousness for the past decade. She holds a Masters Degree in Consciousness and Transformative Studies and a Graduate Certificate in Ecotherapy from John F Kennedy University and is currently in training to become a Certified Somatic Experiencing Practitioner. She was introduced to Thomas Hübl’s work in 2014 and signed up for the first TWT in the US. She is currently the Associate Director of Engagement at the Institute of Noetic Sciences (IONS) where she produces events joining…

leaders.name: Thomas Stelling
leaders.bio: Thomas Stelling lives in Germany where he is working as a certified trainer for Nonviolent Communication (CNVC), as coach and mediator. He is a senior student of Thomas Huebl, whom he got to know 2007 and soon became a participant of a Timeless Wisdom Training (TWT 1). He was also a participant of the first Pocket Project in Israel 2017/2018 dealing with collective trauma bringing people from 36 countries together. 2018-2021 he was studying developmental trauma with Laurence Heller, the founder of NARM. Thomas is interested in the repercussions of the holocaust in Germany, and is hopeful…

il-transcending-societal-expectations-fo.about: Our relationship to ourselves is impacted by many internalized constructs and cultural beliefs: the messages received early in our family and environment, norms promoted on body aesthetics, the anti-aging culture and pressure to look young, the expectation to get married and have children, the expectations on women in business, amongst others. We would like to go on a journey together to explore and unpack some of these constructs while doing embodiment practices as a way to land fully in and listen to the wisdom of our bodies. We will be building resources to support this embodiment journey.
il-transcending-societal-expectations-fo.invitation: We invite women to explore and integrate various aspects of their relationship with themselves through different moments of life in the context of societal expectations: including body image struggles; relationship with food, illness and disability, pleasure and desire; navigating menopause and the anti-aging culture, etc. Participants are welcomed to choose one specific aspect to explore and use the lab process to get more clarity on the wisdom of their bodies to deal with their challenges. At…
il-transcending-societal-expectations-fo.methods: Each lab session has some components of: (1) Building cohesion and refining our capacity for our exploration; (2) Building resources individually and collectively; (3) Building a reference map of what our field is inviting for healing, (4) Deepening our exploration on different topics brought by the group intelligence. We propose anchoring the lab exploration in a creative process of building an…
il-transcending-societal-expectations-fo.availability: We will meet on zoom once a month (120 min) for the Lab exploration. Lab dates: Jan 19*, Feb 16, Mar 15, Apr 19, May 24, Jun 21, Jul 19, Aug 16, Sep 13, Oct 25, Nov 22, Dec 13. Time: 9-11am pst/12-2pm est/6-8pm cet. *The first lab session (Jan 19) is the only that will happen one hour later…

leaders.name: Adriana Mascolli Fontes
leaders.bio: Adriana is an experienced group facilitator, executive coach and somatic therapist. She has been studying with Thomas Hübl since 2016, and served in the GTWT 2022-23 team. She was part of the Pocket Project labs in 2021 co-facilitating: The Legacy of White Privilege in the US and Collective Trauma in Brazil. She is currently a graduate student on Somatic Psychology at CIIS (California). She graduated from the Somatic Blueprint (TM) from the Ray Castellino Foundation (Prenatal-Birth Therapy). Originally from Sao Paulo, Brazil; currently based in California. Coming more fully into her body is a…

leaders.name: Monica Clare
leaders.bio: Monica Clare combines her financial experience as a CPA with her numerous leadership and family office coaching designations to deliver a unique message about money and its impacts. An expert in psychological safety, she shares her insight and deep wisdom to help families as they navigate financial matters. Monica is a global consultant specializing in conflict management through strategic leadership for private enterprises, public companies, governments, and associations. Monica is a Certified Professional Co-Active Coach, a Certified Professional Accountant and a Family Enterprise Advisor…

il-lebanon-a-nexus-of-collective-trauma-.about: Moving from Trauma-Inducing to Trauma-Informed to Trauma-Integrating Cultures. We turn towards realising, recognising and acknowledging the specific expression of ancestral and collective fields of trauma in Lebanon. In this Lab, we begin by forming coherence and resourcing the group, before we turn towards the specific area of trauma that we are focussing on. We address trauma fields identified with the group, e.g. anxiety of Lebanese and in the Lebanese society. Each journey has its own quality and rhythm, which we need to attune and adapt to, thus shaping a unique learning experience.
il-lebanon-a-nexus-of-collective-trauma-.invitation: We can be touched in many ways by the devastating situation Lebanon finds itself in at present. Your background may be of Lebanese origin, living in Lebanon or abroad, you may have Lebanese ancestors in your family lines or other connections and curiosities related to Lebanon. You are all very welcome to join our journey for a year. As we focus on dynamics in the Lebanese experience, we do this here without the participation of holders of the Israeli citizenship with respect to the present…
il-lebanon-a-nexus-of-collective-trauma-.methods: We will go by the CTIP (https://pocketproject.org/download/8119/) and will adapt to the flow and needs of the group. We invite you to maintain/prioritise your own presence in the group field, even in triggering or challenging moments. - to give time, attention and love to this journey also in everyday life - to contribute to the surveys to support the scientific research of our lab - to work in…

leaders.name: Frank Behrens
leaders.bio: Frank Behrens became a trained process engineer after being magically attracted by the processual journey of transformation processes, deeply inspired and often excited about the way technical processes can be designed. Most recently, as a freelance sales engineer in international sales, Frank has been experiencing the call to change direction for more than 13 years. Today he offers coaching, mentoring and mediation for those facing life-changing situations. Each new journey he faces with amazement and wonderment, knowing that the process will make his next step clear.

leaders.name: Flavia Valgiusti
leaders.bio: Flavia Valgiusti is an international expert in Trauma-Informed Law and Director of the Institute of Neurosciences and Law at the Bar Association of San Isidro, Argentina. She works as a UNICEF consultant supporting the development of trauma-informed legal frameworks, recent projects in North Macedonia. A lawyer, social psychologist, and specialist in criminal law, she is also a Professor of Criminology and Neurosciences and served as a Juvenile Court Judge. Her work integrates law, neuroscience, and trauma studies to strengthen justice systems through rights-based and humane approaches.

leaders.name: Spozhmay Orlya
leaders.bio: Spozhmay Oriya studied in Afghanistan and has a BA in psychology and MA in Education. She was assistant professor at faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences, Kabul University for 15 years. Teaching experience in Kabul education university, Kabul medical university and others as a couple of research with national and international researchers. Currently she is a PhD candidate at the faculty of education, Simon Fraser University in Vancouver, Canada. The focus of her research is meaning of collective trauma of war and its societal impacts from perspective of Afghan refugees.

il-healing-collective-grief-suppression.about: This lab is designed to create a collective space to identify and process the cumulative effects and suppressed grief caused by modern day life. We will share in witnessing its impacts, especially those prioritizing efficiency, productivity, competition and domination at the expense of human and ecological well being, and social connection. Through communal witnessing we seek to metabolize the frozen energies into a fluid and vibrant resource for the individual and collective.
