il-healing-collective-grief-suppression.invitation: We invite anyone: -Feeling called to identify and process modern day grief and trauma with communal support. -Wanting to increase awareness of their patterns eroding relationships and impacting their quality of life. -Wanting a safe and intimate space for collectively grieving. -Feeling overwhelmed by the speed of life; seeking more self-regulation. -Grieving, for example: climate destruction, loss of natural habitats, political upheaval, polarization, etc -Wanting to touch the pain within your…
il-healing-collective-grief-suppression.methods: Each Lab offers a theme that aligns our collective focus, bringing participants deeper into their felt senses. We will observe the pace of our habitual reactions, and learn to slow down in order to cultivate curiosity and intimacy with self. We will create an intentional space for expression, expand our awareness of the individual in relationship to the collective, and the interdependence of…

leaders.name: Suresh Schlanger
leaders.bio: Suresh Schlanger is a Trauma Informed Life Coach and Group Facilitator. He has trained in Hakomi Somatic Therapy, Iyengar Yoga, and Ayurvedic Studies. Studying with Thomas Hubl since 2021, Suresh completed the Timeless Wisdom Training in 2023, and is an alumni of the Transparent Communication Leadership Program. He recently completed the Collective Trauma Facilitation Training with Thomas Hubl, as well as Grief Ritual Training for the Climate Aware with Francis Weller. Suresh loves the natural world, gardening, meditation, travel, and playing Native American Flute and hand drums.

leaders.name: Marna Chester
leaders.bio: Marna Chester, raised in NYC and now based in Israel, is a visual artist, Certified Core Energetics Practitioner, and yoga/meditation instructor. A graduate of the Timeless Wisdom Training (2024) and Collective Trauma Facilitator Training (2025), she has supported individuals, couples, and groups since 2018. Her work invites a return to wholeness—where mind, body and soul meet.

leaders.name: Markus Bomm
leaders.bio: Markus is a licensed psychologist and psychotherapist who runs his own private practice in Koblenz. He is trained in various therapeutic approaches and has specialized in trauma therapy in recent years (e.g. PITT, NARM, ...) He has gained broad experience in a variety of settings, including clinics, counseling centers, and addiction services. For over ten years, he accompanied the dying and their families in a hospice. He is studying intensively with Thomas and now supports various courses as a member of the team. He loves being in nature and he is a passionate table-tennis-player.

il-from-polarization-to-sacred-polaritie.about: Please note: To encourage a balance of men and women in this lab, we are now only accepting applications from men. We will explore masculine/feminine polarization and the individual, ancestral, and collective gender wounds that live in our bodies, psyches, relationships, and systems across cultures. We will explore how these wounds manifest in our individual and collective lives — from the most intimate spaces of self and sexuality to the vast arenas of public discourse, political ideologies, and institutional structures. We aim to bring curiosity and awareness to symptoms which include compromised attunement to self and other; distortion of authenticity; and diminished capacities.
il-from-polarization-to-sacred-polaritie.invitation: Men and women who recognize the significance of these wounds in individual and collective life and are ready to bring curiosity, courage, creativity, and vulnerability to to this work. Our intention is to meet the roots of gender polarization and create a space where men and women can be fully seen, wholeness and shared humanity can be recovered, and new possibilities for healing, trust, and authentic relating can take root. Our intention is to bring courage, compassion, curiosity, and a…
il-from-polarization-to-sacred-polaritie.methods: Our exploration will begin with individual experience and progress to collective realities. This is collective shadow work in service of cultural transformation, with implications not only for our inner lives and intimate relationships, but for future generations, societies, and the natural world. Our exploration will begin with individual experience and progress to collective realities. Through…
il-from-polarization-to-sacred-polaritie.availability: Starting on March 8, we will meet on the second Sunday of each month from 10 am- 12 pm PST through December 2026, for a total of 10 sessions.

leaders.name: Krista Bremer
leaders.bio: Krista is an author and facilitator whose writing has appeared in the New York Times, O: the Oprah Magazine, and on NPR. For the past five years she has studied healing practices with Thomas Huebl. She is particularly interested in group process work and tapping the healing power of collective spaces to address the growing mental health crisis, challenge hyperindividualism, and rebuild community. Her interest in gender-related trauma arises from her own life experience and her awareness that her own healing in this realm is connected to the healing of others.

leaders.name: Karl Steyaert
leaders.bio: Karl supports people and organizations to thrive, fulfill their highest potential, and contribute to the greater good. For over 25 years he has facilitated transformation – offering coaching, training, group process & conflict facilitation around the world. A Certified Trainer in Nonviolent Communication (NVC) and a trained Internal Family Systems practitioner, Karl has also undergone intensive training with Arnold Mindell, Collective Trauma facilitation with Thomas Hübl, and Aletheia Coaching. He founded the Cultural Catalyst Network, a global community of changemakers, in 2013.

leaders.name: Lee Morgan
leaders.bio: Lee Morgan is an Osteopath trained in Manual Therapy who works in private practice with children and adults. She has been seeing clients and teaching workshops for more than thirty years. In addition to Osteopathy, her work incorporates somatic and mind-body therapies, including Feldenkrais®, Body-Mind Centering®, and Gyrokinesis®. Her work centers embodiment as a pathway for transformation, empowering her clients to awaken to their original and potential wholeness. Over the last 6 years, Lee has studied a trauma-informed somatic approach influenced by the work of Thomas Huebl.

il-habitando-el-cuerpo-latinoamericano.about: Si has sentido dolor por tu territorio y te abruma o te conmueve la fragmentación, la violencia, la polarización y las heridas heredadas que cargamos en Latinoamérica, este Laboratorio te invita a crear espacio para exhalar el estrés crónico, explorar con cuidado lo que duele y reconectar con lo vivo en ti y en lo colectivo. Buscamos integrar, desde nuestro cuerpo, comportamientos colectivos que hemos normalizado y que generan miedo, desconfianza, escasez e insensibilidad.
il-habitando-el-cuerpo-latinoamericano.invitation: Para participantes comprometidos a un año de exploración profunda, dispuestos a cultivar la observación consciente y practicar la presencia relacional. Este laboratorio da la bienvenida a quienes estén dispuestos a abordar las heridas colectivas y ancestrales de Latinoamérica con curiosidad, valentía y compasión, en un espacio confidencial y de respeto mutuo. Practicaremos la responsabilidad y la humildad para asumir nuestra sombra y el papel que desempeñamos en las dinámicas…
il-habitando-el-cuerpo-latinoamericano.methods: Practicaremos ejercicios para cohesionarnos como grupo, identificar patrones de ausencia, negación y fragmentación, regular nuestro sistema nervioso y acompañarnos en lo que surja momento a momento, apoyándonos de fortalezas culturales latinoamericanas como calidez, solidaridad, creatividad, humor y cuidado mutuo. Nos enfocaremos en restaurar nuestra capacidad de sentir, sintonizarnos…
il-habitando-el-cuerpo-latinoamericano.availability: Nos reuniremos virtualmente los viernes, durante 2 horas, los días 6 y 27 de marzo, 10 de abril, 8 y 22 de mayo, 12 de junio, 3 de julio, 14 de agosto, 11 de septiembre, 2 y 16 de octubre y 13 de noviembre a las 12 p. m. hora de Guatemala, 1 p. m. hora de Ecuador-Colombia y 3 p. m. hora de…

leaders.name: Stephanie Pizarro
leaders.bio: Stephanie Pizarro es colombiana, coach de equipos ejecutivos, educadora experiencial y docente de escuelas de negocios, con experiencia en Liderazgo Transformacional, Desarrollo Organizacional y Gestión del Cambio. Apoya iniciativas regenerativas centradas en el cuidado mutuo. Autora de “Al baño María”, guía para mujeres en autoconocimiento y propósito. Comunicadora Social, con Maestrías en Responsabilidad Social Corporativa y Ciencia Interna, y cursa un doctorado sobre facilitación del trauma colectivo.

leaders.name: Maria Soledad Troya
leaders.bio: María Soledad Troya es ecuatoriana, Coach Ontológico Profesional y Somatic Experiencing Practitioner, acompaña a líderes ejecutivos y grupos de organizaciones multiculturales en su desarrollo de liderazgo, facilitando un trabajo transformacional muy profundo. Combina su trabajo con su experiencia en emprendimiento, liderazgo de Coaches, facilitadora de grupos, meditadora, deportista, estudiante, esposa, y madre de tres hijos. Tiene un título en Administración de Empresas en The University of Texas at Austin y está certificada en Conscious Business Coaching.

leaders.name: Karla Mejia
leaders.bio: Psicoterapeuta salvadoreña especializada en la integración del trauma individual y colectivo, con más de 15 años de experiencia en las Américas y Europa. Terapeuta y facilitadora en integración de trauma en El Salvador, Belice y Guatemala con comunidades indígenas, garífunas y ladinas afectadas por las guerras civiles. Comunidades afectadas por la pobreza extrema, inmigración. Líder de programas de trauma colectivo para adolescentes en contextos de alta violencia. Posee una licenciatura en Psicología, una maestría en Psicología Analítica Transpersonal, formación en EMDR, AIT y Radiónica.
